title: DataQualityDashboardDimensionAndPieReindexUIIT fails on every PR since #31662 changed the Entity Health pie URL to testCaseStatus[]=
body:
## Describe the bug

Every PR whose head contains #31662 (`feat(ui): add multi-select test case status filter`, `e8ee606439`, merged 2026-08-20 03:42 UTC) fails the `java-playwright-nightly` workflow — checks `ui-it-nightly (elasticsearch)`, `ui-it-nightly (opensearch)` and `Test Report`:

```
[ERROR] DataQualityDashboardDimensionAndPieReindexUIIT.dashboardNavigationSurvivesReindex:92->runDashboardFlow:130 » Timeout Timeout 20000ms exceeded

com.microsoft.playwright.TimeoutError: Timeout 20000ms exceeded
	at com.microsoft.playwright.impl.FrameImpl.waitForURLImpl(FrameImpl.java:1110)
	at org.openmetadata.playwright.ui.pages.DataQualityDashboardPage.clickPieChartSegmentExpectsStatusNav(DataQualityDashboardPage.java:71)
	at org.openmetadata.playwright.scenarios.observability.DataQualityDashboardDimensionAndPieReindexUIIT.runDashboardFlow(DataQualityDashboardDimensionAndPieReindexUIIT.java:130)
	at org.openmetadata.playwright.scenarios.observability.DataQualityDashboardDimensionAndPieReindexUIIT.dashboardNavigationSurvivesReindex(DataQualityDashboardDimensionAndPieReindexUIIT.java:92)
```

This is deterministic, not flaky. The workflow checks out `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`, so each run tests its own branch's code. Comparing every recent nightly run's head against `e8ee606439`:

| nightly conclusion | branch | contains #31662 |
|---|---|---|
| success | `hangzhou` | no |
| success | `hangzhou` | no |
| success | `fix/domain-hard-delete-asset-reindex-28923` | no |
| success | `claude/slack-thread-review-c0d314` | no |
| failure | `dependabot/.../slack-github-action-4.0.0` | yes |
| failure | `dependabot/.../actions/cache-6` | yes |
| failure | `harshach/rdf-fidelity` | yes |
| failure | `pmbrull/ai-entities-vector-embeddings` | yes |
| failure | `pmbrull/ai-entities-vector-embeddings` (after a main bump) | yes |

9/9. Merging `main` does not help — it is what introduces the failure.

## Root cause

#31662 changed the Entity Health pie's segment→status mapping from one status per segment to several:

```ts
-export const BINARY_STATUS_PIE_SEGMENT_ORDER: TestCaseStatus[] = [
-  TestCaseStatus.Success,
-  TestCaseStatus.Failed,
+export const BINARY_STATUS_PIE_SEGMENT_ORDER: TestCaseStatus[][] = [
+  [TestCaseStatus.Success, TestCaseStatus.Queued],
+  [TestCaseStatus.Failed, TestCaseStatus.Aborted],
 ];
```

`EntityHealthStatusPieChartWidget` passes that through `getTestCaseTabPath` → `getTestCaseListPath`, which serializes with `qs.stringify(..., { arrayFormat: 'brackets' })`. The redirect URL therefore went from

```
/data-quality/test-cases?testCaseStatus=Failed
```

to

```
/data-quality/test-cases?testCaseStatus%5B%5D=Failed&testCaseStatus%5B%5D=Aborted
```

which `EntityHealthStatusPieChartWidget.test.tsx` asserts in the same PR.

`DataQualityDashboardPage.java:71` still waits on the old shape:

```java
page.waitForURL(
    Pattern.compile("/data-quality/test-cases.*testCaseStatus="),
    new Page.WaitForURLOptions().setTimeout(20_000));
```

`testCaseStatus` is no longer followed by `=`, so `waitForURL` never resolves and the step times out after 20s.

Only step 3 of `runDashboardFlow` breaks:

- step 2 (Test Case Result pie) still passes — `TEST_CASE_STATUS_PIE_SEGMENT_ORDER` stayed scalar, so it still emits `testCaseStatus=Failed`;
- step 4 (Data Assets Coverage) still passes — it only asserts `/data-quality/test-suites`, with no status param.

The URL change is intended product behaviour, so the IT contract is what needs updating, not the UI.

## To Reproduce

1. Open any PR whose head contains `e8ee606439`.
2. Wait for `java-playwright-nightly`.
3. `ui-it-nightly (elasticsearch)` and `ui-it-nightly (opensearch)` both fail with the timeout above.

## Expected behavior

`clickPieChartSegmentExpectsStatusNav` asserts the navigation contract ("the click navigated to the test-cases route with a status filter") and should accept both the scalar and the bracketed-array encodings of `testCaseStatus`.

## Version

- OpenMetadata `main` (2.0.0-SNAPSHOT), from 2026-08-20 onwards.

## Additional context

The 2.0 line is **not** affected yet, but only incidentally: `openmetadata-collate@2.0` pins its `OpenMetadata` submodule at `a6212af` (2026-08-18, #31606), which predates #31662, and `openmetadata-collate@main` pins `f293caf` (2026-08-10). The 2.0 Java UI IT nightly runs `DataQualityDashboardDimensionAndPieReindexUIIT` and it passes there for that reason. The same failure will appear on 2.0 as soon as either submodule pin moves past `e8ee606439`.

title: MCP error responses serialize the McpError exception — unauthenticated 401 leaks a full Java stack trace
body:
## Summary

An unauthenticated `POST /mcp` returns a **13.8 KB JSON body containing a full 60-frame Java stack trace**. `McpError` extends `RuntimeException`, and we hand the exception object itself to Jackson, so the serialized form carries `stackTrace`, `cause`, `suppressed` and `localizedMessage` straight to anonymous callers.

This blocks the Claude Directory / ChatGPT app submissions: `/mcp` unauthenticated is the *first* request a reviewer makes, and "meet Anthropic's security standards" is submission requirement #1.

## Reproduce

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://<tenant>.getcollate.io/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
```

Verified live on `devrel` 2026-08-21 → `HTTP/2 401`, `content-length` 13874.

Body keys: `cause`, `stackTrace` (60 frames), `jsonRpcError`, `message`, `suppressed`, `localizedMessage`.

Leaked frames include our own class/file/line layout, the Jetty/Dropwizard/servlet internals and the exact JRE build:

```
io.modelcontextprotocol.spec.McpError$Builder.build(McpError.java:72)
org.openmetadata.mcp.server.transport.OAuthHttpStatelessServerTransportProvider.sendAuthErrorWithChallenge(OAuthHttpStatelessServerTransportProvider.java:451)
org.openmetadata.mcp.server.transport.OAuthHttpStatelessServerTransportProvider.authenticateRequest(OAuthHttpStatelessServerTransportProvider.java:392)
org.openmetadata.mcp.server.transport.HttpServletStatelessServerTransport.doPost(HttpServletStatelessServerTransport.java:147)
...
org.eclipse.jetty.util.thread.QueuedThreadPool$Runner.run(QueuedThreadPool.java:1194)
java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:1583)   ← moduleName "java.base", moduleVersion "21.0.12"
```

## Root cause

Two sites serialize the `McpError` **exception** rather than its JSON-RPC error payload:

1. `openmetadata-mcp/.../transport/OAuthHttpStatelessServerTransportProvider.java:451-452` — the auth path.

   ```java
   McpError error = McpError.builder(McpSchema.ErrorCodes.INTERNAL_ERROR).message(message).build();
   String jsonError = getObjectMapper().writeValueAsString(error);
   ```

2. `openmetadata-mcp/.../transport/HttpServletStatelessServerTransport.java:250-259` — `responseError(...)`, same pattern, which covers **every** 400/500 path in `doPost`. Those are authenticated-only, but one of them is `"Unexpected error: " + e.getMessage()`, so an authenticated caller gets both an internal exception message and a stack trace.

## Secondary problems on the same response

- **Wrong message when no credentials were sent.** With no `Authorization` header at all the body says `"Invalid or expired token"`. Per RFC 6750 §3 those are distinct cases — no credentials is not an invalid token, and the wording sends integrators hunting for a bad token they never had.
- **Wrong JSON-RPC code.** `-32603 INTERNAL_ERROR` for an auth failure. Nothing internal failed.
- **`WWW-Authenticate` never carries `error="invalid_token"`.** `sendAuthErrorWithChallenge` only appends an `error` parameter for 403/`insufficient_scope`. RFC 6750 §3.1 wants `error="invalid_token"` on the 401-with-a-bad-token case (and correctly *omits* it when no credentials were supplied — that half is already right).

The header side is otherwise in good shape: `www-authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…/mcp/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource", scope="openid profile email"` is exactly what the MCP spec asks for.

## Expected

A bare, RFC-shaped error envelope and nothing else:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32001,"message":"Missing or invalid bearer token"}}
```

`McpError` already exposes `getJsonRpcError()` (`{code, message}`) — serialize that inside a `JSONRPCResponse`, never the throwable. Stack traces belong in `LOG.debug`, which `authenticateRequest` already does.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No `stackTrace` / `cause` / `suppressed` / `localizedMessage` key in any `/mcp` response body, at any status code, authenticated or not.
- [ ] `responseError(...)` in `HttpServletStatelessServerTransport` fixed too — not just the auth path.
- [ ] Missing-credentials vs invalid-token distinguished in the message, with an auth-appropriate JSON-RPC code instead of `-32603`.
- [ ] `error="invalid_token"` added to `WWW-Authenticate` when a token was supplied and rejected; still absent when no credentials were sent.
- [ ] Regression test asserting the unauthenticated 401 body against the exact expected JSON, so this cannot silently come back.
- [ ] `"Unexpected error: " + e.getMessage()` reviewed — internal exception text should not reach the wire either.

title: Looker connector: Column level lineage missing for quoted column names
body:
### Connector

Looker

### Feature area

Lineage

### Describe the bug

When parsing the SQL column names from the LookML views, the Looker connector uses a regex to detect the table column: https://github.com/open-metadata/OpenMetadata/blob/main/ingestion/src/metadata/ingestion/source/dashboard/looker/metadata.py#L875

However, this regex does not handle quotes (`"`) around the column name, which can be used in Snowflake to handle case issues in the column names or column names with e.g. spaces. For example, the Looker connector is able to parse `${TABLE}.CUSTOMER_ID` just fine, but fails to find the column name for `${TABLE}."CUSTOMER_ID"` or `${TABLE}."Customer Id"`.

### To Reproduce

Create a LookML view with a `sql: {TABLE}."MY_COLUMN"` entry.

title: PII: numeric column values are never matched by pattern recognizers
body:
### Affected module

Governance (Glossary / Classification / Domains)

### Describe the bug

Values from numeric columns are captured into sample data, but are never evaluated by pattern recognizers. PII stored in a numeric column (national IDs, employee numbers, phone numbers) is therefore invisible to content-based classification, no matter how the recognizer is configured.

### To Reproduce

In an Oracle database, a table or view exposes the same employee identifier twice, once as `NUMBER` and once as `VARCHAR2(9)`. `GET /api/v1/tables/{id}/sampleData` returns:

```
columns: ['hr_person_id', 'employee_pri']
row[0]:   hr_person_id = 77046931   (int)
          employee_pri = '77046931' (str)
```

After Auto Classification with a `target: content` pattern recognizer (`^0?\d{8}$ / \b0?\d{8}\b`):

Column | Source type | Sample value | Result
-- | -- | -- | --
employee_pri | VARCHAR2(9) | '77046931' (str) | PII.Sensitive applied
hr_person_id | NUMBER | 77046931 (int) | no tag

Same value, same row, same table, same run, same recognizer. The only difference is that the sampler delivers one as a Python `str` and the other as an `int`.

### Expected behavior

Numerical values must be checked by classifiers too.

This is a significant false-negative class for PII discovery. Identifiers that are conceptually sensitive are routinely stored as numeric types: social insurance/social security numbers, employee numbers, phone numbers, account numbers. In our case the same sensitive identifier is correctly flagged in its `VARCHAR2` column and silently missed in its `NUMBER` column. The numeric one is arguably the more important of the two, since it is the primary key used across joins.

Coerce sample values to their string representation before handing them to the analyzer, so numeric columns are scanned like textual ones. If numeric exclusion is intentional (e.g., for performance), it should at minimum be documented and ideally configurable, since it silently defeats PII detection for a large and common category of sensitive data.

### OS

Kubernetes

### Python version

3.10.19

### OpenMetadata version

1.12.14

### OpenMetadata Ingestion package version

1.12.14.2

### Additional context

### Suspected cause
Presidio's `PatternRecognizer` operates on text. If sample values are handed to the analyzer without being coerced to `str`, numeric values either raise silently, are skipped, or never match. The sampler clearly does not exclude numeric columns: they are present in `sampleData.columns` with their values, so the gap appears to be in the classification step, not the sampling step.

title: PII: classification recognizers with target: "column_name" never produce a match
body:
### Affected module

Governance (Glossary / Classification / Domains)

### Describe the bug

With Issue #31845  worked around (all recognizers set to `"supportedLanguage": "en"`, matching the pipeline), target: "content" recognizers work correctly. However, no target: "column_name" recognizer has ever produced a match in our environments, neither our custom ones nor the built-in system defaults shipped with the installation.

### To Reproduce

View `stg.sap_pme_test_pii_v` (Oracle view, sample data captured successfully, 803 rows in source):

Column | Type | Result
-- | -- | --
employee_pri | varchar2(9) | `PII.Sensitive` applied. `labelType: Generated`, `source: Classification`, via a `target: content` pattern recognizer
first_name | varchar2(40) | no tag, despite built-in `person` recognizer (`target: column_name, regex ^.*(user\|client\|person\|first\|last\|maiden\|nick).*(name).*$, isSystemDefault: true`, enabled)
last_name | varchar2(40) | no tag, same recognizer should match
hr_person_id | number | no tag, our custom `exact_terms` `column_name` recognizer lists `hr_person_id` verbatim in `exactTerms`
middle_name, initials, known_as | varchar2 | no tag

The successful `employee_pri` tag in the same table and run establishes that the table was in scope, sample data was available, the classification engine ran, the confidence thresholds were satisfiable, and the tag write path worked. The only recognizers that failed are the `column_name` ones.

We also tested a `column_name exact_terms` recognizer whose `exactTerms` contained the exact, complete column name (case-insensitive via `regexFlags.ignoreCase: true` because Oracle stores identifiers uppercase), the most favourable possible input for that type with `confidenceThreshold` lowered to 0.05 gave no match.

No `Classification PII (mutually exclusive): Selected...` log line is ever emitted for a `column_name` recognizer, suggesting these recognizers are not evaluated rather than evaluated and rejected on score.

### Expected behavior

Classification recognizers based on columns' name should tag the column as PII when there is an exact match.

### OS

Kubernetes

### Python version

3.10.19

### OpenMetadata version

1.12.14

### OpenMetadata Ingestion package version

1.12.14.2

### Additional context

### Ruled out before filing
- Filter patterns: log shows the table in records, not filtered.
- Source permissions/sample data: sample data present and non-empty, verified in UI.
- Stale entity state: table/view hard-deleted and recreated from scratch (new id, version: 0.1); no change. Also reproduced on a brand-new view never previously ingested.
- Sample data caching: `DELETE /api/v1/tables/{id}/sampleData` then re-run; no change.
- Confidence thresholds: tested with recognizer `confidenceThreshold: 0.05` and `patterns[].score: 0.99`, `Classification.autoClassificationConfig.minimumConfidence: 0.6`. An extreme margin changes nothing.
- `isSystemDefault`:  tested both `true` and `false` on custom recognizers; no difference. Built-in `isSystemDefault: true` `column_name` recognizers also fail.
- `supportedLanguage`: Issue #31845 above; all recognizers now set to "en" matching the pipeline, which fixed content recognizers but not `column_name` ones.
- Recognizer type: failed with both `pattern` and `exact_terms` configs.
- Schema validity: configs validated against published JSON schemas. An earlier invalid submission was correctly rejected by client-side Pydantic validation (missing required `regexFlags`), so we know malformed configs do surface errors.

### Possible lead
#25720 changed recognizer-to-tag association to use the tag's `fullyQualifiedName` as a registry key (`self.recognizers[tag_fqn] = ...`) with `_find_matching_tags` comparing `tag.fullyQualifiedName == entity_type`. We were unable to inspect the recognizer-loading code path (`tag_processor.py` and the column-name scanning branch) to determine whether `column_name` recognizers are registered and dispatched through the same mechanism as content ones, or whether that branch is reached at all.

### Pre-submission checklist

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues.
- [x] I removed credentials, hostnames, emails, and other sensitive data from logs and config.

title: PII: `"supportedLanguage": "any"` silently disables a custom recognizer
body:
### Affected module

Governance (Glossary / Classification / Domains)

### Describe the bug

## Summary
`classificationLanguages.json` offers "any" as a valid enum language value, described as applying the recognizer regardless of configured language. In practice, a recognizer with `"supportedLanguage": "any"` is never evaluated: no match, no tag, no warning, no error. The pipeline reports Success: 100%, Errors: 0, Updated records: 0.

Setting the same recognizer's supportedLanguage to "en", matching the pipeline's `sourceConfig.config.classificationLanguage`, makes it work immediately, with no other changes.

### To Reproduce

1. Add a recognizer to `PII.Sensitive` via JSON PATCH (Content-Type: application/json-patch+json) with supportedLanguage: "any":
```json
{
  "name": "test_content_digits",
  "enabled": true,
  "confidenceThreshold": 0.5,
  "target": "content",
  "recognizerConfig": {
    "type": "pattern",
    "supportedLanguage": "any",
    "patterns": [{ "name": "digits8", "regex": "\\b\\d{8}\\b", "score": 0.5 }],
    "regexFlags": { "dotAll": true, "multiline": true, "ignoreCase": true },
    "context": ["employee", "person"]
  }
}
```
2. Run Auto Classification against a table with a varchar column containing 8-digit values → no tag applied.
3. PATCH only `/recognizerConfig/supportedLanguage` to "en", change nothing else, re-run → tag applied correctly (`labelType: Generated`, `source: Classification`).

### Expected behavior

"any" is the natural choice for recognizers that are inherently language-independent: national ID formats, postal codes, telephone numbers or any `column_name` recognizer, where "language" is not a meaningful attribute. The schema advertises it, the API accepts it, and the recognizer then silently never fires. This is very hard to diagnose: nothing in the logs distinguishes "recognizer not loaded" from "recognizer loaded but matched nothing".

### Suggested fix
- Either honour "any" by registering the recognizer under every configured language (or bypassing the language filter for it), or reject the value at validation time with a clear error if it cannot be supported.
- Improve the documentation on classification language support

### OS

Kubernetes

### Python version

3.10.19

### OpenMetadata version

1.12.14

### OpenMetadata Ingestion package version

1.12.14.2

### Additional context

### Suspected cause
Presidio's `RecognizerRegistry` selects recognizers by exact language-code equality against the language argument of `AnalyzerEngine.analyze()`. Presidio has no "any" concept, so a recognizer registered under language "any" is never selected for an "en" run. The value appears to be accepted and persisted by the API/schema without ever being translated into something Presidio can act on.

title: Domain-scoped non-admin users blocked from Services list and Ingestion Runner field despite correct backend permissions
body:
### Affected module

UI

### Describe the bug

Two related UI permission-gating bugs prevent domain-scoped non-admin users from accessing features that the backend already permits. Direct API testing (GET/POST) confirms correct backend permission enforcement in both cases below — these are frontend-only defects.

1. Database Services list page shows "No permission"
A non-admin user with a `hasDomain()`-scoped `ViewAll` permission on `databaseService` sees "No permission" when navigating to Settings → Services → Databases, even though their domain matches services in the list.

2. Ingestion Runner dropdown never renders for non-admins
In the create/edit database service form, the "Ingestion Runner" dropdown never renders for a non-admin user, at any permission level (unconditional, +ViewBasic, hasDomain()-scoped, fully unconditional).

### To Reproduce

Bug 1:
1. Create a role with `ViewAll` on `databaseService`, scoped via a `hasDomain()` condition.
2. Assign the role to a non-admin user in that domain.
3. Log in as that user and navigate to Settings → Services → Databases.
4. Observe "No permission" error, despite `GET /permissions` returning `conditionalAllow` and matching services existing in the domain.

Bug 2:
1. As a non-admin user with create/edit permission on a database service (any grant level), open the create or edit service form.
2. Observe the "Ingestion Runner" dropdown is not shown, at any permission level.
3. Directly POST a service payload with `ingestionRunner` and `domains` set as this non-admin user — the request succeeds and both fields persist.

### Expected behavior

1. The Services list page should render and show services within the user's domain when the backend permission is `conditionalAllow`, with visibility of individual services still governed by domain-scoping at the instance level.
2. The Ingestion Runner field should render based on the user's actual permission to create/edit the service, not a hardcoded admin check.

body:
### Affected module

UI

### Describe the bug

Team user management doesn't behave consistently depending on team type. For Group teams, everything works as expected — you can add, remove, and export users normally. For Department, Division, and BusinessUnit teams, none of that holds up, and a user can end up in a state where they're stuck on the team with no way to remove them.

1. Export comes back empty. The team export CSV doesn't contain users when the team is of type non-Group (Department/Division/BusinessUnit). If such a team has users, exporting it produces a CSV with no user data — every time, regardless of how many members the team actually has.
2. No way to add a user through the UI. The Add User option simply isn't available for non-Group teams.
3. A user can still end up on the team anyway — for example via a direct API update — and once there, they show up correctly in the Users tab. But trying to remove them through the UI fails with:

`Team is of type Department. Users can be updated only in team of type Group.`

And trying to fix it by changing the team's type to Group also fails if the team has any sub-teams, with:

`A team with children cannot be updated to type Group.`

### To Reproduce

1. Take a Department-type team that has sub-teams under it.
2. Get a user added directly to that team (e.g. via API).
3. Confirm the user shows up correctly in the team's Users tab.
4. Try to remove that user via the UI — fails with the error above.
5. Try converting the team to Group to work around it — also fails, since it has sub-teams.
6. Export the team — the resulting file has no users in it, despite the team clearly having a member.

### Expected behavior

Team membership behavior (add, remove, export) should be consistent across all team types — a user who can be added should also be removable and exportable, regardless of whether the team is Group, Department, Division, or BusinessUnit.

title: Tag propagation cascade: delete not symmetric with add; column list/get API missing inherited Derived tags
body:
# Table Tag Delete Cascade + Column API Missing Derived Tags

## Summary
Table tag propagation to child docs (columns, test suites) works on ADD but breaks on DELETE. Column list/get API also fails to return inherited Derived tags.

## Bug A: Delete cascade doesn't propagate tag removal to children

**Symptom:** Remove a glossary term from a table via Assets tab (or via table PATCH removing the tag). Table's own doc updates. Column ES docs still hold the Derived tag. Same for test_suite/test_case ES docs.

**Repro:**
1. Create Glossary + GlossaryTerm.
2. Create Table with columns.
3. Tag the Table with the term.
4. Verify column ES doc has term as `Derived` tag ✓.
5. Go to Glossary Term → Assets tab → delete the table asset.
6. Query column ES doc → still has the Derived tag. Phantom.

**Expected:** Column/testSuite/testCase ES docs lose the Derived tag when the parent Table's tag is removed.

**Files to check:**
- `openmetadata-service/src/main/java/org/openmetadata/service/jdbi3/GlossaryTermRepository.java` — bulk remove asset flow
- `openmetadata-service/src/main/java/org/openmetadata/service/search/SearchRepository.java:3069` — TAG_LABEL_LIST delete script wiring
- `openmetadata-service/src/main/java/org/openmetadata/service/search/SearchRepository.java:2504` — `propagateInheritedFieldsToChildren`

**Root cause hypothesis:** Remove-asset flow calls `searchRepository.updateEntity(asset)` without a ChangeDescription that has `fieldsDeleted=[tags]`, so `requiresPropagation` returns false → delete cascade never runs.

**Fix direction:** Ensure remove-asset path emits proper ChangeDescription with `fieldsDeleted` including tags, OR directly invoke propagation with synthesized ChangeDescription.

## Bug B: List/GET column API missing inherited Derived tags

**Symptom:** ES doc for a column has parent-table's tag as `Derived`. API response (`GET /tables/{fqn}?fields=tags,columns`) returns column with only its own tags — parent-inherited Derived tags absent.

**Impact:** UI column tag panel doesn't show inherited term. Explore card + Assets tab show it (from ES). Divergence.

**Expected:** API returns `column.tags = [own tags] + [parent Table's tags with labelType=DERIVED]`.

**Files to fix:**
- `openmetadata-service/src/main/java/org/openmetadata/service/Entity.java:993` — `populateEntityFieldTags`
- `openmetadata-service/src/main/java/org/openmetadata/service/jdbi3/TableRepository.java:201` — `setFields`

**Fix direction:** In column tag population, also fetch parent Table's tags, mark them as `DERIVED`, dedup by tagFQN, append to each column's `tags`.

## Bug C: Playwright test asserts wrong count

**File:** `openmetadata-ui/src/main/resources/ui/playwright/e2e/Pages/Glossary.spec.ts:1197`

**Current:**
```ts
await goToAssetsTab(page, glossaryTerm1.data.displayName, 1);
```

**Actual:** count = 1 + `<number of top-level columns propagated>` + 0 (no test_suite in this test)

**Fix:** Update assertion to expected count including inherited column entries, OR change assertion to verify presence of the table card by testid without asserting exact count.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Removing a tag from a Table (via API PATCH removing tag, and via Glossary Term Assets tab remove) removes the Derived tag from all descendant column/testSuite/testCase ES docs.
- [ ] `GET /tables/{fqn}?fields=tags,columns` returns columns with parent-Table tags marked `labelType=DERIVED`.
- [ ] CSV export of Table columns includes the inherited Derived tags.
- [ ] Playwright Glossary "Assign Glossary Term to entity and check assets" test asserts the correct expanded count OR uses card-visibility assertion.
- [ ] IT covers: tag Table → column ES has Derived; column API has Derived; remove tag → column ES cleared; column API cleared.
- [ ] One-time cleanup: strip orphan `Derived` tags from `column_search_index`, `test_suite_search_index`, `test_case_search_index`, `test_case_resolution_status_search_index`, `test_case_result_search_index` for tags whose parent no longer holds them.

## Related PR
Introducing PR: https://github.com/open-metadata/OpenMetadata/pull/26901 (April 3 2026, TAG_LABEL_LIST propagation descriptor added on TableRepository).

## Priority
High — user-visible divergence between column entity page (no inherited tag shown) and Assets tab / Explore (shows column). Broken delete cascade means phantom tags accumulate.

title: dbt relationships test: entity_link resolves to wrong table when model alias differs from model name
body:
### Affected module

Ingestion Framework

### Describe the bug

### Environment
  - OpenMetadata Server: 1.13.1
  - OpenMetadata Ingestion (client): 1.13.1.1
  - dbt adapter: dbt-spark (Iceberg tables on AWS S3 Tables)

  ### Description
  When a dbt project uses `config(alias=...)` to give a model a physical table
  name different from its dbt model name (e.g. model file `silver__foo.sql` with
  `config(alias='foo')`), OpenMetadata's dbt ingestion attaches column-level
  `relationships` test cases to the WRONG table — the referenced/target table
  instead of the table actually under test — causing a `400 Invalid column name`
  error and the test case is never created.

  ### Root cause
  `generate_entity_link()` extracts the "primary table" for a relationships test
  from `test_metadata.kwargs['model']` via a regex on the `ref(...)` call. This
  `ref()` call always contains the dbt **model name** (e.g. `silver__foo`).
  
  Meanwhile, in `dbt_metadata.py`, `parse_upstream_nodes()` builds the candidate
  `upstream_list` FQNs using `get_dbt_model_name()`, which returns the model's
  **alias** when set (e.g. `foo`, without the `silver__` prefix) — not the model
  name.
  
  `generate_entity_link()` then does:
      if fqn.endswith(f".{primary_table_name}"):
          primary_table_fqn = fqn

  Since `primary_table_name` (from the model name, e.g. `silver__foo`) can never
  match an FQN built from the alias (e.g. `...foo`), this comparison always
  fails — for every relationships test on this project's models, not just some.
  The code then silently falls back to `upstream_list[0]`, which for a
  relationships test is the referenced/parent model listed first in
  `depends_on.nodes` — the wrong table.

  ### Repro
  1. dbt model `silver__child.sql`:
     {{ config(alias='child') }}
     select ... as _child_fk ...
  2. schema.yml:
  ```yaml
  - name: _child_fk
    tests:
    - relationships:
        arguments:
          to: ref('silver__parent')
          field: _parent_sk
  3. silver__parent.sql also uses config(alias='parent').
  4. Run the dbt ingestion workflow against manifest.json + run_results.json.
  5. Observe: Failed to ingest CreateTestCaseRequest [...] due to api request failure: Invalid column name _child_fk — because the entity link resolved
  to parent (which has _parent_sk, not _child_fk) instead of child.

  Suggested fix

  In generate_entity_link(), compare primary_table_name (extracted from the
  ref() model name) against the upstream nodes' dbt name attribute (or the
  raw manifest node), not against the alias-derived FQN — or resolve
  kwargs['model'] through the same alias-aware path used in
  parse_upstream_nodes(), so the two are consistently comparable.

### To Reproduce

 1. Create a dbt model `silver__child.sql` with an explicit alias stripping a
     layer prefix from the physical table name:

         {{ config(alias='child') }}
         select ... as _child_fk ...

  
         {{ config(alias='parent') }}
         select ... as _parent_sk ...

  3. In schema.yml, add a column-level `relationships` test on `_child_fk`:

         - name: _child_fk
           tests:
           - relationships:
               arguments:
                 to: ref('silver__parent')
                 field: _parent_sk

  4. Run `dbt build` to produce manifest.json + run_results.json, upload them to
     the S3 prefix configured for OpenMetadata's dbt ingestion, and run the dbt
     ingestion workflow (dbtConfigType: s3) against a database service where
     both `child` and `parent` tables are already catalogued (e.g. via the
     Athena connector).
  5. Check the ingestion logs.

### Expected behavior

The relationships test case should be created on the table actually under
  test (`child`, which has the `_child_fk` column), as a Test Case attached to
  that table's entity, with a passing/failing testCaseResult depending on the
  dbt test outcome.
  
  Instead, ingestion logs:

      Failed to ingest CreateTestCaseRequest
      [relationships_silver__child___child_fk__ref_silver__parent_]
      due to api request failure: Invalid column name _child_fk
      
  The test case is never created, because generate_entity_link() resolves the
  entity link to the PARENT table (`parent`) instead of `child` — see the root
  cause analysis in the issue description (dbt_utils.py / dbt_metadata.py name
  vs. alias mismatch).

### OS

title: Incident Manager: truncated table name has no usable tooltip (native `title` only, dead `??` fallback)
body:
### Affected module

UI

### Describe the bug

In **Observability → Incident Manager**, the **Table** column truncates long table names with a CSS ellipsis but gives no usable tooltip on hover, so the full name is unreachable.

The cell is [`IncidentManagerTable.component.tsx:182-196`](https://github.com/open-metadata/OpenMetadata/blob/main/openmetadata-ui/src/main/resources/ui/src/components/IncidentManager/IncidentManagerTable.component.tsx#L182-L196):

```tsx
<Table.Cell>
  <Link
    className="tw:inline-block tw:max-w-52 tw:truncate tw:align-middle"
    data-testid="table-link"
    title={getNameFromFQN(tableFqn) ?? ref?.fullyQualifiedName}
    to={getEntityDetailsPath(...)}>
    {getNameFromFQN(tableFqn) ?? ref?.fullyQualifiedName}
  </Link>
</Table.Cell>
```

There are three separate defects here.

**1. Wrong tooltip mechanism.** The only tooltip is the bare native `title` attribute. Native `title` is browser/OS-rendered: it has a ~1s delay, is unstyled, is **not shown on keyboard focus**, and is suppressed entirely on touch devices. Hiding truncated content behind it fails [WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.13 (Content on Hover or Focus)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus.html) and looks broken next to the rest of the app.

The sibling table in the same module already does this correctly — [`DataQualityTab.tsx:465-477`](https://github.com/open-metadata/OpenMetadata/blob/main/openmetadata-ui/src/main/resources/ui/src/components/Database/Profiler/DataQualityTab/DataQualityTab.tsx#L465-L477) wraps truncated cell content in `Tooltip` + `TooltipTrigger` from `@openmetadata/ui-core-components`. The convention exists; this cell just never got it.

**2. The `??` fallback is dead code, and the tooltip can be empty.** `getNameFromFQN(fqn: string): string` ([`FqnUtils.ts:117`](https://github.com/open-metadata/OpenMetadata/blob/main/openmetadata-ui/src/main/resources/ui/src/utils/FqnUtils.ts#L117)) always returns a string — never `null`/`undefined` — so `?? ref?.fullyQualifiedName` can never fire.

When `ref.fullyQualifiedName` is absent, `getPartialNameFromTableFQN` returns `''`, then `getNameFromFQN('')` returns `''`. Result: the link renders with **no visible text and no tooltip at all**, and the intended fallback to the full FQN silently never happens. This needs `||`, not `??`.

**3. The tooltip should show the full FQN, not the bare table name.** Both the visible text and the tooltip currently resolve to the same value — the last FQN segment. So even when the native tooltip does appear, it adds nothing beyond untruncating the same string. The tooltip is the right place to show the qualified path (`service.database.schema.table`) so the user can tell two same-named tables apart.

### To Reproduce

1. Create test cases on tables with long names (e.g. `pw-table-eb16dd75-b2d6-4a3f-…`) and open incidents on them.
2. Go to **Observability → Incident Manager**.
3. The **Table** column shows truncated names ending in `…`.
4. Hover a truncated name — no styled tooltip appears (only the delayed, unstyled native one).
5. Tab to the link with the keyboard — nothing appears at all.

### Expected behavior

- Hovering **or keyboard-focusing** a truncated table name shows the design-system `Tooltip` (`Tooltip` + `TooltipTrigger` from `@openmetadata/ui-core-components`), matching `DataQualityTab`.
- The tooltip shows the **full qualified table path**, not just the last segment.
- When the test case reference has no `fullyQualifiedName`, the cell falls back to something meaningful instead of rendering blank.

### OS

macOS 15 (browser-agnostic — reproduces in Chrome, Safari, Firefox)

### Python version

N/A (UI only)

### OpenMetadata version

`main` / 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT

### OpenMetadata Ingestion package version

N/A (UI only)

### Additional context

**Introduced in** #29744 (`2c4df74457`, *"refactor(dq): extract test case & test suite detail page hooks…"*), which added the `tw:truncate` class and the `title` attribute in the same hunk.

**A test currently locks in the weak behavior** and must be updated as part of the fix — [`IncidentManagerTable.component.test.tsx:295-300`](https://github.com/open-metadata/OpenMetadata/blob/main/openmetadata-ui/src/main/resources/ui/src/components/IncidentManager/IncidentManagerTable.component.test.tsx#L295-L300):

```ts
it('should truncate the table link and expose the full name via title', () => {
  ...
  expect(tableLink).toHaveAttribute('title', 'NameFromFQN');
});
```

Replace the `title`-attribute assertion with one that asserts the `Tooltip` renders, and add a case covering the missing-`fullyQualifiedName` path from defect 2.

**Scope for a first-time contributor:** one cell in one component, one operator fix (`??` → `||`), plus the two test updates above. No schema, backend, or API changes.

title: Bedrock model id carries a hardcoded eu. inference-profile prefix, so LLM calls fail outside EU regions
body:
The Bedrock LLM config defaults `modelId` to `eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`. That leading `eu.` is a cross-region inference profile prefix and it has to match the region the client actually talks to. Any deployment outside the EU that keeps the default, or copies a model id from another environment, gets `Bedrock completion failed` on every call.

It is easy to hit and slow to diagnose. The region comes from a separate setting, the model id looks perfectly valid, and the only signal is a generic Bedrock error surfacing in whatever feature made the call (we hit it through NLQ filter extraction, which just stops resolving filters).

The client already receives the AWS region when it is built, so the prefix should not be something operators keep in sync by hand. Proposal: when the configured model id carries no geo prefix, derive it from the region; when it carries one, leave it alone. Pair that with a region-neutral default so a fresh deployment does not start out broken.

This mapping already exists in Collate's agent platform, which resolves the prefix from the region at model-resolution time. Putting it in OSS means one implementation both sides use instead of two copies drifting apart.

title: Knowledge page approval tasks are orphaned: KnowledgePageRepository still closes and re-assigns through the legacy feed path
body:
## Summary

`KnowledgePageRepository` is the only entity repository still driving approval tasks through the
pre-redesign feed path, in two places:

- `closeApprovalTask(Page, String)` closes through `FeedRepository.getTask` + `closeTask`.
- `updateTaskWithNewReviewers(Page)` re-assigns by patching the legacy `Thread` through
  `FeedRepository.patchThread`, and on top of that is invoked from nowhere, unlike the five
  repositories that wire their counterpart into the reviewers-changed update path.

Approval tasks are `Task` entities now, so the feed lookup never matches: the open `Task` is
orphaned whenever a page leaves review without its task being resolved through the task API, and a
reviewer change while a review is open never reaches the task's assignees.

Verified on `main` at `9ad7ad848e` (2026-08-18).

## The code

**Closing:**

```java
// jdbi3/KnowledgePageRepository.java:839-856
private void closeApprovalTask(Page entity, String comment) {
  MessageParser.EntityLink about = new MessageParser.EntityLink(KNOWLEDGE_PAGE_ENTITY, entity.getFullyQualifiedName());
  FeedRepository feedRepository = Entity.getFeedRepository();
  ...
  Thread taskThread = feedRepository.getTask(about, TaskType.RequestApproval, TaskStatus.Open);
  feedRepository.closeTask(taskThread, entity.getUpdatedBy(), new CloseTask().withComment(comment));
}
```

Called from `postUpdate` on three transitions: approved (`:820`), rejected (`:822`) and back to
DRAFT (`:833`). Since nothing creates thread-tasks for pages any more, `feedRepository.getTask`
throws `EntityNotFoundException`, which is caught and logged as "No approval task found for page".

**Re-assigning:**

```java
// jdbi3/KnowledgePageRepository.java:752-778
protected void updateTaskWithNewReviewers(Page page) {
  ...
  Thread originalTask = feedRepository.getTask(about, TaskType.RequestApproval, TaskStatus.Open);
  ...
  feedRepository.patchThread(null, originalTask.getId(), updatedTask.getUpdatedBy(), patch);
}
```

Same dead lookup, same swallowed `EntityNotFoundException`. And it is dead code twice over: where
`TagRepository:1083`, `TestCaseRepository:1714`, `DataProductRepository:960`,
`DataContractRepository:1434` and `MetricRepository:482` call their override from an
`updateReviewers()` hook in the entity updater, nothing calls this one, so knowledge pages have no
reviewer-to-assignee sync even of the broken kind.

## The migrated counterparts

For closing, `GlossaryTermRepository` has the identical private method, already migrated:

```java
// jdbi3/GlossaryTermRepository.java:1708
private void closeApprovalTask(GlossaryTerm entity, String comment) {
  TaskRepository taskRepository = (TaskRepository) Entity.getEntityRepository(Entity.TASK);
  taskRepository.closeApprovalTaskForEntity(
      entity.getFullyQualifiedName(), entity.getUpdatedBy(), comment);
}
```

`TaskRepository.closeApprovalTaskForEntity` documents itself as "the replacement for
`feedRepository.getTask()` + `feedRepository.closeTask()` pattern used by entity repositories when
an entity's approval status changes". Also adopted by `TagRepository:1307`,
`TestCaseRepository:1971`, `DataProductRepository:1267`, `DataContractRepository:1839`,
`MetricRepository:709` and `AutoApproveServiceTaskImpl:51`.

For re-assigning, `TagRepository` is the wired exemplar:

```java
// jdbi3/TagRepository.java:1078-1085 (in TagUpdater)
@Override
public void updateReviewers() {
  super.updateReviewers();
  if (original.getReviewers() != null
      && updated.getReviewers() != null
      && !original.getReviewers().equals(updated.getReviewers())) {
    updateTaskWithNewReviewers(updated);
  }
}

// jdbi3/TagRepository.java:1311
protected void updateTaskWithNewReviewers(Tag tag) {
  ...
  taskRepository.updateApprovalTaskAssignees(
      tag.getFullyQualifiedName(), new ArrayList<>(tag.getReviewers()), tag.getUpdatedBy());
}
```

`TaskRepository.updateApprovalTaskAssignees` (`TaskRepository.java:1377`) documents itself as "used
when an entity's reviewers change while an approval task is in progress" and is null-safe when no
open task exists.

## Impact

In the normal flow the task is already closed by `PUT /v1/tasks/{id}/resolve`, so
`closeApprovalTask` acts as a safety net. It matters when a page's approval status changes
*without* the task being resolved:

- the page is sent back to DRAFT while a review is open, which is exactly the case the method's own
  TODO describes;
- the status is patched directly rather than through the task.

In those cases the `Task` stays `Open` indefinitely: it keeps appearing in assignee inboxes and task
counts, and a later review round starts with a stale task attached to the page.

The reviewer half never runs at all, so whether a reviewer change reaches the open task depends
entirely on the page's approval workflow. Neither `openmetadata-service` nor `collate-service`
seeds one for `knowledgePage`, so it is customer-defined: if it uses an `eventBasedEntity` trigger
on `Updated`, `CreateTask` supersedes the open task on the next run and the new reviewers inherit a
fresh task; if it does not, nothing updates the assignees and the task stays with the old reviewers.
Either way the repository contributes nothing, and in the superseding case the task id changes
under the reviewer instead of being patched in place. Same shape as #31692 on
`GlossaryTermRepository`, except that glossary at least has a seeded workflow doing the masking.

## Fix

1. Swap `closeApprovalTask` to `TaskRepository.closeApprovalTaskForEntity`, mirroring
   `GlossaryTermRepository`. The replacement is null-safe ("Silently does nothing if no open task
   exists"), so the surrounding `try` / `EntityNotFoundException` handling can go with it.
2. Swap `updateTaskWithNewReviewers` to `TaskRepository.updateApprovalTaskAssignees` and wire it
   into the page updater's `updateReviewers()` the way `TagRepository` does, so the method stops
   being dead code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `KnowledgePageRepository.closeApprovalTask` closes through `TaskRepository.closeApprovalTaskForEntity`.
- [ ] `KnowledgePageRepository.updateTaskWithNewReviewers` re-assigns through `TaskRepository.updateApprovalTaskAssignees` and runs when a page's reviewers change.
- [ ] Sending a page in review back to DRAFT leaves no open `Task` for that page, covered by a test.
- [ ] Changing reviewers while a page review is open updates the open task's assignees, covered by a test.
- [ ] No `FeedRepository` task call (`getTask`, `closeTask`, task-thread `patchThread`) remains in any entity repository.

## Related

Prerequisite for #30559 Phase 3, which deletes the `FeedRepository` task surface (including
`closeTask`) outright. That issue tracks the full retirement of the legacy thread-task model; this
one is a standalone bug and does not depend on it.

title: dbt ingestion does not create/update testCaseResult for tests with status "pass" in run_results.json
body:
### Affected module

Data Quality / Profiler

### Describe the bug

When ingesting dbt test results via the dbt ingestion workflow (manifest.json + run_results.json + catalog.json, dbt Core artifacts sourced from S3), OpenMetadata only creates a testCaseResult on the corresponding test case entity when the dbt test status is "fail". Test cases whose dbt result is status: "pass" never receive a testCaseResult at all — the field is completely absent from the API response (not present as null, not present as an empty object), and the test case shows no status in the UI.

This affects both dbt generic/schema tests (not_null, unique) and would presumably affect singular tests as well, since the behavior tracks status, not test type. Confirmed via a controlled experiment: taking a run_results.json where a specific generic test (not_null on a column) had status: "pass", message: null, failures: 0, and manually flipping only that one result to status: "fail" with a non-null message and failures: 1 (all other fields, timestamps, and invocation_id left untouched) caused OpenMetadata to create a testCaseResult for that test case on the next ingestion run — where previously (with status: "pass") none existed.

This means:

Data Quality dashboards built from dbt test results only ever show failures, never confirmation that a test is passing.
A test that previously failed and later passes will retain its stale "Failed" testCaseResult indefinitely, since no new result is ever written to supersede it — creating a false impression that a resolved issue is still active.

### To Reproduce

Set up a dbt project with a mix of generic tests (not_null, unique) that pass and a custom singular test that fails.
Run dbt build to generate manifest.json and run_results.json (same invocation).
Run dbt docs generate to produce catalog.json.
Upload all three artifacts to S3.
Configure and run the OpenMetadata dbt ingestion workflow (S3 source) pointing at these artifacts.
Query the ingested test cases via GET /api/v1/dataQuality/testCases?fields=testCaseResult (or view them in the UI under the table's Data Quality/Observability tab).
Observe: test cases corresponding to status: "fail" dbt results have a populated testCaseResult with testCaseStatus: "Failed". Test cases corresponding to status: "pass" dbt results have no testCaseResult field at all, and show no status in the UI.
To confirm the trigger is specifically status, take the same run_results.json, flip one passing test's status to "fail" (add a message and non-zero failures, leave everything else — including unique_id, timestamps, and invocation_id — unchanged), re-upload to the same S3 path, and re-run the ingestion. The previously-blank test case now receives a testCaseResult with testCaseStatus: "Failed".

### Expected behavior

OpenMetadata should create/update a testCaseResult for every dbt test result in run_results.json, regardless of whether status is "pass", "fail", or "error". A passing test should produce a testCaseResult with testCaseStatus: "Success" (mirroring how OpenMetadata's own native profiler tests behave), so that:

The Data Quality dashboard accurately reflects current pass/fail state for all tests, not just failures.
A test that transitions from failing to passing gets a new "Success" result that supersedes the old "Failed" one, rather than leaving a stale failure visible indefinitely.

### OS

_No response_

### Python version

_No response_

### OpenMetadata version

_No response_

### OpenMetadata Ingestion package version

_No response_

### Additional context

OpenMetadata version:
1.13.0 (server), confirmed via GET /api/v1/system/version. Behavior also verified present using dbt Core 1.8.0 artifacts (run-results/v6.json schema). Not yet tested against 1.13.1–1.13.3, though changelog review of those patch releases found no related fix.

title: OpenMetadata metadata disappears from UI after Docker restart and Data Quality Test Suites do not execute
body:
### Affected module

Backend

### Describe the bug

## Description

I am running OpenMetadata 1.12.6 in a Docker Compose environment and I am experiencing two major issues.

The first and more critical issue is that OpenMetadata metadata appears to disappear from the UI after stopping and restarting the Docker environment.

The second issue is that Data Quality Test Suites can be created successfully but are not executed and do not produce test results.

These issues may be related to the state/persistence of the OpenMetadata metadata database, ingestion service, or Airflow environment.

---

## Environment

- OpenMetadata Server: 1.12.6
- OpenMetadata Ingestion: 1.12.6
- OpenMetadata DB image: 1.12.6
- Elasticsearch: 7.17.26
- Source Database: PostgreSQL 16
- OpenMetadata metadata database: MySQL
- Airflow: 3.1.5
- Deployment: Docker Compose

Docker containers:

- openmetadata_server: docker.getcollate.io/openmetadata/server:1.12.6
- openmetadata_ingestion: docker.getcollate.io/openmetadata/ingestion:1.12.6
- openmetadata_mysql: docker.getcollate.io/openmetadata/db:1.12.6
- openmetadata_elasticsearch: docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch:7.17.26
- demo-postgres: postgres:16

---

# 1. Metadata disappears after Docker restart

I create and configure metadata in OpenMetadata, including:

- Database Services
- Glossary
- Glossary Terms
- Data Quality Test Cases
- Test Suites
- Metrics
- Domains and other metadata

After stopping the Docker environment and starting it again after some time, OpenMetadata frequently appears as if it has been reset.

Previously created objects are no longer visible in the UI.

However, the metadata does not appear to be completely deleted from the backend.

For example, a Database Service may disappear from the UI, but when I try to create a new Database Service with the same name, OpenMetadata reports that the entity/service already exists.

This makes it appear that the entity still exists in the backend but is not correctly visible or indexed in the UI.

The behavior is especially noticeable after the Docker environment has been stopped for several days and then started again.

I did not intentionally delete the metadata or the database.

### Expected behavior

Metadata created in OpenMetadata should persist after stopping and restarting the Docker Compose environment.

Previously created entities should remain visible and usable after the containers are restarted.

### Questions

Could this behavior be related to:

- Docker volume persistence
- MySQL metadata database persistence
- Elasticsearch persistence/index state
- OpenMetadata server state
- Elasticsearch reindexing
- Docker Compose configuration
- Any known issue in OpenMetadata 1.12.6?

---

# 2. Data Quality Test Suite does not execute

I also have a problem with the Data Quality functionality.

I can successfully create Data Quality Test Cases and a Test Suite for a PostgreSQL table.

For example, I created test cases for:

- PostgreSQL table: DEMO-PSQL.postgres.public.customers
- Column-level data quality tests
- Regex-based validation tests
- Other table/column-level test scenarios

The Test Suite is successfully created in the UI and an active schedule can be configured.

However, the tests are not executed and no test results are generated.

The UI shows:

- Total Tests: 0
- Successful Tests: 0
- Failed Tests: 0
- No Last Run result

The Test Suite appears to exist, but the workflow does not actually execute.

---

## Airflow / Ingestion investigation

I checked the OpenMetadata ingestion container.

The generated DAG files exist under:

`/opt/airflow/dags`

and generated Test Suite configuration files exist under:

`/opt/airflow/dag_generated_configs`

For example, the generated Test Suite configuration contains:

- `pipelineType: TestSuite`
- `enabled: true`
- `pausePipeline: false`
- `scheduleInterval: "0 0 * * *"`

However, the generated configuration also contains:

`"deployed": false`

When I try to inspect the Airflow DAGs using:

`docker exec openmetadata_ingestion airflow dags list`

Airflow returns:

`ERROR: You need to initialize the database. Please run 'airflow db migrate'. Make sure the command is run using Airflow version 3.1.5.`

The ingestion container itself is running.

The generated DAG Python file is also present and references the generated Test Suite configuration.

---

## PostgreSQL connection

The PostgreSQL database connection from OpenMetadata is mostly successful.

The connection test reports successful results for:

- CheckAccess
- GetDatabases
- GetSchemas
- GetTables
- GetViews
- GetTags
- GetColumnMetadata
- GetTableComments
- GetInformationSchemaColumns

The only warning observed during the connection test is related to query collection:

`Failed to fetch queries, please validate if postgres instance has pg_stat_statements extension installed and the user has at least select privileges for pg_stat_statements table.`

The PostgreSQL service itself is reachable and table metadata can be successfully retrieved.

Therefore, this `pg_stat_statements` warning does not appear to explain why Data Quality Test Suites are not executing.

---

# Expected behavior

1. OpenMetadata metadata should persist across Docker Compose restarts.
2. Existing metadata should remain visible in the UI.
3. Entities should not remain in the backend while becoming invisible/unavailable in the UI.
4. Data Quality Test Suites should be deployed successfully.
5. Scheduled Test Suites should execute.
6. Test results should be generated and displayed in the OpenMetadata UI.

---

# Questions

Could you please help us determine:

1. Why does OpenMetadata metadata become invisible after restarting the Docker environment while attempting to recreate the same entity results in an "already exists" error?

2. Is this related to MySQL/Elasticsearch persistence or indexing?

3. Is there any known issue with metadata persistence in OpenMetadata 1.12.6 when deployed using Docker Compose?

4. Why is the Test Suite pipeline generated with `"deployed": false`?

5. Is the Airflow error requiring `airflow db migrate` related to the Test Suite workflow not being deployed/executed?

6. Is Airflow 3.1.5 fully supported/configured correctly with OpenMetadata 1.12.6 Data Quality workflows?

7. Is there any recommended Docker Compose configuration or volume configuration to ensure that OpenMetadata metadata and Data Quality workflow state persist across container restarts?

Any guidance on the recommended configuration or troubleshooting steps would be appreciated.

### To Reproduce

### Environment

- OpenMetadata: 1.12.6
- Deployment: Docker Compose
- OpenMetadata Server: 1.12.6
- OpenMetadata Ingestion: 1.12.6
- OpenMetadata DB: 1.12.6
- Elasticsearch: 7.17.26
- Airflow: 3.1.5
- Source PostgreSQL: 16

### Issue 1 – Metadata becomes unavailable after Docker restart

1. Start the OpenMetadata Docker Compose environment.
2. Create metadata such as a Database Service, Glossary, Glossary Terms, Metrics and Data Quality Test Cases.
3. Verify that these objects are visible and usable in the OpenMetadata UI.
4. Stop the Docker environment.
5. Leave the environment stopped for several days.
6. Start the Docker environment again.
7. Open OpenMetadata and check the previously created metadata.

After the restart, previously created metadata may no longer be visible in the UI.

However, the entities do not appear to be completely deleted from the backend. For example, attempting to create a Database Service using the same name can result in an "already exists" error even though the service is not visible in the UI.

### Issue 2 – Data Quality Test Suite does not execute

1. Create a PostgreSQL Database Service and ingest the metadata successfully.
2. Create a Data Quality Test Case for a PostgreSQL table/column.
3. Create a Test Suite and add the test cases.
4. Configure the Test Suite as an active scheduled workflow.
5. Wait for the scheduled execution or attempt to execute the workflow.
6. Check the Data Quality / Test Suite results.

The Test Suite does not execute and no test results are generated.

The generated DAG and Test Suite configuration files are present inside the `openmetadata_ingestion` container.

The generated configuration contains `"enabled": true` and `"pausePipeline": false`, but `"deployed": false`.

Additionally, running `airflow dags list` inside the ingestion container returns:

`ERROR: You need to initialize the database. Please run 'airflow db migrate'. Make sure the command is run using Airflow version 3.1.5.`

### Expected behavior

### Expected behavior

1. Metadata created in OpenMetadata should persist after stopping and restarting the Docker Compose environment.
2. Previously created entities should remain visible and accessible in the OpenMetadata UI after a restart.
3. An entity should not be invisible in the UI while still existing in the backend and causing an "already exists" error when recreated.
4. Data Quality Test Suites should be successfully deployed and executed according to their configured schedule.
5. Data Quality test results should be generated and displayed in the OpenMetadata UI.
6. Restarting the Docker environment should not cause the OpenMetadata metadata state or Data Quality workflow state to become inconsistent.

### OS

Windows 11 (Docker Desktop / WSL2)

### Python version

3.10.19

### OpenMetadata version

1.12.6

### OpenMetadata Ingestion package version

openmetadata-ingestion==1.12.6

### Additional context

### Deployment

OpenMetadata is deployed using Docker Compose on Windows 11 through Docker Desktop / WSL2.

- OpenMetadata Server: 1.12.6
- OpenMetadata Ingestion: 1.12.6
- OpenMetadata DB: 1.12.6
- Elasticsearch: 7.17.26
- Source PostgreSQL: 16

### Docker containers

- openmetadata_server
- openmetadata_ingestion
- openmetadata_mysql
- openmetadata_elasticsearch
- demo-postgres

The OpenMetadata server and Elasticsearch containers are running and healthy.

The PostgreSQL connection from OpenMetadata is also mostly successful. CheckAccess, GetDatabases, GetSchemas, GetTables, GetViews, GetTags, GetColumnMetadata, GetTableComments and GetInformationSchemaColumns are successful.

The only connection warning is related to fetching query history because the PostgreSQL `pg_stat_statements` extension is not installed. This does not appear to prevent metadata ingestion.

The main issues are:

1. Metadata becomes unavailable/invisible in the UI after restarting the Docker environment, while attempting to recreate the same entity can result in an "already exists" error.
2. Data Quality Test Suite workflows are generated but are not executed and no test results are produced.
3. The generated Test Suite configuration contains `"deployed": false`.

title: Team userCount goes stale/inflated after user removal, reassignment, or deactivation
body:
### Affected module

Search / Discovery

### Describe the bug

Total User Count Staleness — after removing/reassigning a user from a team (via UI or API) or if user is deactivated, userCount stays stale/inflated while the Users list correctly updates. Reproducible via both direct API PATCH and Team UI actions.

RCA —

Deactivated user:
getUserCount() counts raw relationship rows with no status filter. getUsers() (Users list) filters via NON_DELETED. So a deactivated user's relationship row stays uncounted-out in the list but still counted in userCount.

Reassigned/moved user:
Team-side removal doesn't delete relationships directly — it diffs origTeam.getUsers() (old state) against the new submitted list, and only removes what's flagged as deleted in that diff. origTeam.getUsers() is fetched via the same getUsers()/findTo() call already known to be unreliable (e.g. empty for space-named teams). If it fails to return a user who's actually still a member, the diff never marks them as removed, so the relationship row never gets deleted — userCount stays inflated even though the UI shows a clean removal.

### To Reproduce

Path 1 — Deactivated user

1. Add a user to a team so the team's userCount reflects them.
2. Deactivate that user (via Users admin settings or API).
3. Observe: the team's Users list no longer shows the user (correct), but userCount still includes them (stale).

Path 2 — Reassigned/removed user

1. Add a user to Team A so the team's userCount reflects them.
2. Remove or reassign the user to a different team, either via the Team UI (edit team members) or via a direct API PATCH on the team.
3. Observe: the Users list for Team A no longer shows the user (correct), but Team A's userCount still includes them (stale) — because the removal diff against origTeam.getUsers() failed to detect the user as a removal target.
4. Observe: the Users list for Team A no longer shows the user (correct), but Team A's userCount still includes them (stale) — because the removal diff against origTeam.getUsers() failed to detect the user as a removal target.

### Expected behavior

userCount should always match the users actually rendered in the team's Users list, staying in sync after removal, reassignment, or deactivation.

title: Trino: empty column comments ingested as "", and updated column comments ignored with overrideMetadata=true
body:
### Connector

Trino

### Feature area

Metadata ingestion

### Describe the bug

Two defects that together cause Trino column descriptions to silently stop syncing.

**1. Columns with no comment are ingested with an empty-string description**

Trino's `SHOW COLUMNS` reports a column with no comment as the empty string, never `NULL`. `_get_columns` in `ingestion/src/metadata/ingestion/source/database/trino/metadata.py` passes `record.Comment` straight through to `description`, so every uncommented column lands in OpenMetadata with `"description": ""` rather than no description at all. An explicit `COMMENT ''` produces the same value, so the two cases are indistinguishable at that layer.

**2. Updated column comments are not ingested even with `overrideMetadata: true`**

Once a column has a non-empty description, a re-run never updates it. The entity-level `updateDescription()` in `EntityRepository.java` honours the `overrideMetadata` flag, but the column-level `updateColumnDescription()` does not — it unconditionally reverts a bot PUT whenever the stored column description is non-empty. `updateColumnDisplayName()` has the same gap.

The two defects mask each other. A column with no comment is stored as `""`, which is `nullOrEmpty`, so its *first* comment does land — making the sync look functional right up until a second update to an already-described column is silently dropped.

### To Reproduce

**Part 1 — blank descriptions**

1. In Trino, create a table mixing all three comment states:
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE memory.testdb.student_data (
       id BIGINT,
       age INTEGER COMMENT '',
       name VARCHAR COMMENT 'Name of the student'
   );
   ```
2. Run metadata ingestion for the Trino service.
3. Fetch the table's columns from the API. `id` and `age` both come back as `"description": ""` instead of having no description.

**Part 2 — updates dropped**

4. Create a table where one column has a comment and another does not:
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE memory.default.fruits (
       type VARCHAR,
       price DOUBLE COMMENT 'price of fruit'
   );
   ```
5. Run ingestion. `type` is stored as `""`, `price` as `price of fruit`.
6. Change both comments in Trino:
   ```sql
   COMMENT ON COLUMN memory.default.fruits.type IS 'first comment on fruit type';
   COMMENT ON COLUMN memory.default.fruits.price IS 'second comment on fruit type';
   ```
7. Re-run ingestion with `overrideMetadata: true`.
8. `type` updates correctly, but `price` keeps the stale `price of fruit`.

As a control, ingesting the same Trino source into a **brand-new** service produces the correct description for both columns — that path is an insert, so no merge guard runs. This confirms the connector reads the updated comments correctly and the loss is in the server-side column merge, not in extraction.

### Expected behavior

1. A column with no comment in Trino should be ingested with **no description**, not an empty string, so it is not shown as described and does not interfere with later updates.
2. With `overrideMetadata: true`, a changed source comment should overwrite the stored column description, matching the behaviour already provided for the entity-level description.

### Connection / ingestion config

```yaml
source:
  type: trino
  serviceName: <redacted>
  serviceConnection:
    config:
      type: Trino
      hostPort: <redacted>
      username: <redacted>
      authType:
      catalog: memory
  sourceConfig:
    config:
      type: DatabaseMetadata
      overrideMetadata: true
sink:
  type: metadata-rest
  config: {}
workflowConfig:
  loggerLevel: DEBUG
  openMetadataServerConfig:
    hostPort: <redacted>/api
    authProvider: openmetadata
    securityConfig:
      jwtToken: <redacted>
```

### OS

macOS 26.5.1

### Python version

3.11.15

### OpenMetadata version

2.0.0-SNAPSHOT (main)

### Additional context

Root causes located at:

- `ingestion/src/metadata/ingestion/source/database/trino/metadata.py` — `_get_columns` passes the empty-string comment through unchanged. `TRINO_TABLE_COMMENTS` filters `is not null` but not `COMMENT ''`, so the table comment has the same gap.
- `openmetadata-service/src/main/java/org/openmetadata/service/jdbi3/EntityRepository.java` — `ColumnEntityUpdater.updateColumnDescription` / `updateColumnDisplayName` omit the `!overrideMetadata` condition that `updateDescription()` and `updateDisplayName()` both have.

Note that fixing only the ingestion side is not sufficient: it stops new blank descriptions but leaves existing non-empty column descriptions permanently un-updatable by ingestion. Both sides are needed.

I have a fix ready and will open a PR linking this issue.

title: PostgreSQL and Greenplum connectors do not discover materialized views with SQLAlchemy 2.x
body:
### Connector

PostgreSQL, Greenplum

### Feature area

Metadata ingestion

### Describe the bug

Materialized views are never ingested during `DatabaseMetadata` ingestion, even with `includeViews: true`. They are not misclassified as `View` — they are absent from the catalogue entirely, and the run reports success with no warning and no filtered-entity record.

Neither of the two object-enumeration paths reaches them:

- `query_table_names_and_types()` is overridden by both connectors (`postgres/metadata.py`, `greenplum/metadata.py`) and filters `pg_class.relkind IN ('r', 'p', 'f')`, which excludes `'m'`.
- `query_view_names_and_types()` is overridden by neither, so it falls back to the default in `common_db_source.py`, which calls `Inspector.get_view_names()`.

Per the [SQLAlchemy 2.0 reflection docs](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/reflection.html), dialects that previously included materialized views in `get_view_names()` — PostgreSQL among them — no longer do; callers must use `Inspector.get_materialized_view_names()`, which no connector calls. `ingestion/setup.py` pins `sqlalchemy>=2.0.0,<3`, so every supported installation is on the split reflection API and the default view path can no longer see materialized views.

The remaining pieces are already in place: `TableType.MaterializedView` exists in the entity schema, and `get_view_definition` for Greenplum already runs `GREENPLUM_VIEW_DEFINITIONS`, whose filter is `relkind IN ('v', 'm')`. Only the enumeration is missing.

### To Reproduce

1. In PostgreSQL or Greenplum, create a schema with one ordinary table, one plain view and one materialized view:
```sql
CREATE SCHEMA mv_repro;
CREATE TABLE mv_repro.base_table (id int, amount numeric);
CREATE VIEW mv_repro.plain_view AS
    SELECT id, amount FROM mv_repro.base_table;
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_repro.mat_view AS
    SELECT id, sum(amount) AS total FROM mv_repro.base_table GROUP BY 1;
```

2. Confirm the ingestion user can see the materialized view:
```sql
SELECT matviewname FROM pg_matviews WHERE schemaname = 'mv_repro';
-- mat_view
```

3. Run metadata ingestion for that service with `includeTables: true`, `includeViews: true` and `schemaFilterPattern` limited to `mv_repro`

4. List what was ingested into that schema:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" \
  "$OM/api/v1/tables?databaseSchema=<service>.<database>.mv_repro&limit=100"
```

**Result:** `base_table` and `plain_view` are returned, `mat_view` is not. It is not
reclassified as `View` — it does not exist as an entity at all. Searching the index for
`tableType:MaterializedView` returns 0 hits. The ingestion run reports success and emits
no warning and no filtered-entity record for it.

### Expected behavior

Materialized views should be ingested as:

    tableType=MaterializedView

when `includeViews=true`, including columns, schemaDefinition and view lineage.

### Connection / ingestion config

```yaml

```

### Logs

```shell

```

### OS

Linux

### Python version

3.10.20

### OpenMetadata version

1.13.0 

### OpenMetadata Ingestion package version

1.13.0

### Additional context

### Suggested implementation

Override query_view_names_and_types() for PostgreSQL/Greenplum and combine:

- Inspector.get_view_names() -> TableType.View
- Inspector.get_materialized_view_names() -> TableType.MaterializedView

This keeps materialized views under the `includeViews` flag, where they belong.

Please avoid the shortcut of adding `m` to the table-discovery queries: that puts materialized views on the table path, where `includeViews` no longer applies, and it also needs `m` added to `RELKIND_MAP` in `common_pg_mappings.py`, which currently maps only `r`, `p`, `f` and `v`.

title: Grafana connector: panels inside collapsed rows are not ingested
body:
### Connector

Grafana

### Feature area

Metadata ingestion

### Describe the bug

When a Grafana dashboard has a `row` panel that is **collapsed** (`"collapsed": true`), 
the Grafana API returns the child panels nested inside `row.panels`, and they are 
**removed** from the top-level `dashboard.panels` array (this is a known, documented 
Grafana API quirk — see grafana/grafana#20253).

The OpenMetadata Grafana connector iterates only over the top-level 
`dashboard_details.dashboard.panels` array and does not recurse into `row.panels`. 
As a result, any panel that is inside a collapsed row at the time of ingestion is 
silently skipped — it is not created as a Chart entity, and no lineage is extracted 
for it either.

Panels inside **expanded** rows are ingested fine, since Grafana keeps them in the 
top-level array in that case. The bug only manifests for collapsed rows, which makes 
it easy to miss during initial testing.

### To Reproduce

1. In Grafana, create a dashboard with at least one row containing 1+ panels.
2. Collapse the row and save the dashboard.
3. Run the OpenMetadata Grafana metadata ingestion for this dashboard.
4. Check the resulting Dashboard entity in OpenMetadata — the panels that were 
   inside the collapsed row are missing from its chart list.

### Expected behavior

All panels should be ingested as Chart entities regardless of whether the row 
containing them is collapsed or expanded at the time of ingestion.

title: Tableau: table lineage silently dropped when the ingestion account lacks Catalog permissions
body:
### Connector

Tableau

### Feature area

Lineage

### Describe the bug

If the Tableau account lacks permissions on Catalog external assets, the Metadata API still returns `upstreamTables` but nulls `name`, `fullName`, `schema` and `database.name`. Only `id` and `luid` survive.

`_get_database_tables` guards on `if table.name:`, so it never attempts a lookup, falls through to an equally-redacted `referencedByQueries`, and returns `None`.

Result: no Table to DataModel lineage, no warning, and `Success %: 100.0`. Seen in production as 0 of 301 data models with upstream lineage, while all 301 kept their Dashboard edge, columns, and a source table correctly present in the catalog.

### To Reproduce

1. Publish a Tableau workbook over a Databricks table, in a project (not Personal Space).
2. Ingest a Tableau service as a **site admin**. The Table to DataModel edge is created.
3. Ingest a second Tableau service, same site and workbook, as a **user without Catalog external asset permissions** (Explorer with View is enough).
4. No edge, no warning, run reports success.

Running the connector's own `TABLEAU_DATASOURCES_QUERY` against the same workbook as each identity:

| Field | Site admin | Explorer |
|---|---|---|
| `upstreamTables` count | 1 | 1 |
| `id` / `luid` | present | present |
| `name` | `rpt_repro_transfer_out_mv` | **null** |
| `fullName` | `[reporting_prod].[finance].[rpt_...]` | **null** |
| `schema` | `finance` | **null** |
| `database.name` | `reporting_prod` | **null** |
| `fields` / `upstreamColumns` | 5 / 4 | 5 / 4 |

`fields` survive because they belong to the workbook, not to a Catalog asset. That is why the data models look healthy and only the upstream table disappears.

### Expected behavior

The run warns that upstream tables came back without names and that this is likely a permissions problem. Lineage is still not created, which is correct: a table cannot be resolved without a name.

### Connection / ingestion config

```yaml
source:
  type: tableau
  serviceName: <redacted>
  sourceConfig:
    config:
      type: DashboardMetadata
      includeDataModels: true
      lineageInformation:
        dbServicePrefixes: []   # empty, so nothing is narrowing the lookup
```

### Logs

```shell
# Restricted account, successful run, no lineage produced and nothing reported.
[...] ERROR  {test_connections:215} - GetOwners-Unable to fetch Dashboard Owners from tableau
[...] WARNING {test_connections:243} - You might be missing metadata in: GetOwners due to Failed to fetch Workbook Owners, please validate if user has access to fetch Owners
[...] INFO   {logger:222} - Workflow Tableau Summary:
[...] INFO   {logger:222} - Processed records: 321
[...] INFO   {logger:222} - Warnings: 0
[...] INFO   {logger:222} - Errors: 0
[...] INFO   {logger:222} - Success %: 100.0


The `GetOwners` failure is the only hint the account is restricted, and it comes from test-connection, not lineage.
```

### OS

_No response_

### Python version

_No response_

### OpenMetadata version

1.13.3, main (2.0.0-SNAPSHOT)

### OpenMetadata Ingestion package version

openmetadata-ingestion==1.13.3

### Additional context

Proposed fix: when an upstream table arrives with an identifier but no usable name and no queries to fall back on, log a warning and record it on the ingestion status so it shows in the run summary.

> Tableau returned upstream table `<luid>` with no name. The ingestion account likely lacks Tableau Catalog permissions on external assets, so table lineage cannot be built for it.

It cannot create lineage, since the name is the only handle available. It turns a silent zero into a self-diagnosing run.

Related, both different from this and neither fixing it:

- #26161: same symptom, other mechanism. Tableau returns no upstream at all for `.hyper` extracts, rather than redacting names.
- #8494: asks for docs on the permissions the Metadata API needs. This is that gap having silent consequences.
