body:
### Connector

mongodb

### Feature area

Test Connection

### Describe the bug

### Summary
In an enterprise environment, it's common for security controls to be set higher than in other environments.

The following scenario currently causes the mongodb openmetadata connector to fail (even if ingestion would be successful):
- mongodb instance has authentication enabled
- AND the openmetadata ingestion config explicitly filters what DBs, collections, etc are ingested
- AND credentials used for mongodb metadata ingestion does not have permission to run listCollections on all databases on the mongoDB instance.

The root cause appears to be that `test_connection()` in [ingestion/src/metadata/ingestion/source/database/mongodb/connection.py](https://github.com/open-metadata/OpenMetadata/blob/main/ingestion/src/metadata/ingestion/source/database/mongodb/connection.py) doesn't respect the filtering specified in the ingestion config — it blindly attempts to get collections from all databases on the mongodb instance, even when the credentials do not have permission to do so.

Not clear if this is by design (i.e. conscious decision that enumeration of all collections is mandatory), inflexibility of the current connection test framework or a bug / oversight specific to the mongoDB connector.

Current workarounds:
 - grant the user permissions to run listCollections on all databases
 - comment out line 80 in [ingestion/src/metadata/ingestion/source/database/mongodb/connection.py](https://github.com/open-metadata/OpenMetadata/blob/main/ingestion/src/metadata/ingestion/source/database/mongodb/connection.py) (keeps the same security posture on the mongoDB side).

title: Automation fails on glossary terms with commas in names due to search_after pagination bug
body:
## Problem
An automation workflow to update glossary term owners is failing to process all terms. Out of 1863 glossary terms, only 311 are getting updated. The automation fails with an Elasticsearch error during pagination.

## Root Cause
The issue occurs in `SearchUtils.searchAfter` method where `split(",")` is used to parse the search_after cursor. When glossary terms contain commas in their fully qualified names, the split logic breaks pagination.

## Error Details
```
metadata.ingestion.ometa.client.APIError: Search failed due to Request failed: [search_phase_execution_exception] all shards failed | Root cause: [illegal_argument_exception: search_after has 2 value(s) but sort has 1.]
```

The error shows that search_after has 2 values but sort has only 1, indicating the comma in the term name is being incorrectly parsed as a delimiter.

## Expected Behavior
Automation should process all glossary terms regardless of special characters (commas, parentheses, etc.) in their names.

## Actual Behavior
Automation stops processing when encountering glossary terms with commas in their fully qualified names, resulting in incomplete updates.

## Affected Component
- `SearchUtils.searchAfter` method
- Glossary term search pagination logic

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create glossary terms with commas in their names
2. Run an automation workflow filtering on those glossary terms
3. Observe pagination failure during search_after operation

title: [UI] FailedTestCaseSampleData unit test crashes on main — Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext')
body:
## Affected module

UI

## Describe the bug

`yarn test` against `main` crashes inside `FailedTestCaseSampleData.test.tsx` with:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext')
  at Object.useContext (.../openmetadata-ui-core-components/.../node_modules/react/cjs/react.development.js:1618:21)
  at .../openmetadata-ui-core-components/.../dist/SnackbarContent.cjs.js:1:302310

The above error occurred in the <Table> component:
  at className (.../openmetadata-ui-core-components/.../dist/SnackbarContent.cjs.js:1:302232)
  at FailedTestCaseSampleData (.../FailedTestCaseSampleData.component.tsx:68:3)
```

The test was added in PR #27956 and passed in that PR's CI. PR #27985 — merged one day earlier — swapped the component's `Table` import from `antd` → `@openmetadata/ui-core-components`. Neither PR's CI exercised the post-merge state, so the regression slipped onto `main`.

### Root cause

`@openmetadata/ui-core-components` ships a prebuilt CJS bundle resolved against its **own** nested `node_modules/react`, separate from the React copy Jest runs with. When the test renders a real export from the package, two React instances co-exist in the same process; the dispatcher in the package's React copy is `null`, so the first `useContext` call inside the bundle throws.

The test was written when the component still imported `Table` from antd (which has no nested React), so the dual-React condition didn't exist on PR #27956's branch.

## To Reproduce

```bash
cd openmetadata-ui/src/main/resources/ui
yarn install
yarn test --testPathPattern=FailedTestCaseSampleData
```

Result:

```
FAIL  src/components/DataQuality/IncidentManager/FailedTestCaseSampleData/FailedTestCaseSampleData.test.tsx
  ● Test suite failed to run
    TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext')
```

## Expected behavior

The test should pass. The `@openmetadata/ui-core-components` package should not be reachable as a real (un-mocked) dependency inside Jest, or the package should not bundle its own React copy.

## Additional context

### Two-PR interaction (why CI was green on both PRs)

| When | PR | Change | Test outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| May 9, 09:38 | #27985 | Swapped component \`Table\` import: antd → core-ui | No test existed yet; nothing to fail |
| May 10, 11:20 | #27956 | Added the test. On this PR's branch the component still imported antd's Table | Test passed — CI stack shows \`rc-table/lib/Table.js\`, \`antd/lib/spin\` |

Direct evidence — PR #27956's CI log (run `25601970266`):

```
PASS  src/components/DataQuality/IncidentManager/FailedTestCaseSampleData/FailedTestCaseSampleData.test.tsx
  at Table (.../node_modules/rc-table/lib/Table.js:141:25)        ← antd
  at Spin (.../node_modules/antd/lib/spin/index.js)
  at InternalTable (.../node_modules/antd/lib/table/Table.js:39)
  at testCaseData (FailedTestCaseSampleData.component.tsx:60:3)
```

Git auto-merged the two PRs without conflict (different parts of the same file), so no human noticed the interaction.

### Process gap

The `yarn-coverage` workflow uses `pull_request_target` and checks out `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` — i.e. the PR head, not a trial merge with `main`. Two PRs that pass individually can still produce a broken `main` when their changes are logically (not textually) intertwined. Running UI tests against `refs/pull/N/merge` would surface this class of regression pre-merge.

### Suggested fixes

1. **Immediate** — mock `@openmetadata/ui-core-components` in `FailedTestCaseSampleData.test.tsx`. This is the existing convention; ~30 other tests in the repo do the same (`IncidentManager.test.tsx`, `ColumnDetailPanel.test.tsx`, etc.).

2. **Medium-term** — `openmetadata-ui-core-components` should declare `react`/`react-dom` as **peerDependencies only** (not as a direct dependency that gets installed into its own `node_modules`). The `preinstall` script in `openmetadata-ui/src/main/resources/ui/package.json` currently runs `yarn install` inside the core-components package, which creates the nested copy that breaks Jest.

3. **Long-term** — switch `yarn-coverage.yml` to check out the merge ref so PR pairs like #27985 + #27956 are validated together:

   \`\`\`yaml
   - uses: actions/checkout@v4
     with:
       ref: refs/pull/\${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/merge
   \`\`\`

## OS

macOS (also reproduces on Ubuntu CI when running off `main` directly)

## OpenMetadata version

`main` (as of commit 2967a7f0a8 and later)

title: MySQL 5.7+: general_log.argument field type changed from MEDIUMTEXT to MEDIUMBLOB, causing data lineage SQL query failure
body:
### Affected module

Lineage

### Describe the bug

### Description
In MySQL 5.7 and above, the `mysql.general_log.argument` field type was changed from `MEDIUMTEXT` (MySQL 5.6 and earlier) to `MEDIUMBLOB`. This breaks OpenMetadata's data lineage SQL extraction, which relies on querying this field as text. When the field is `MEDIUMBLOB`, lineage analysis fails to parse SQL statements and returns empty or incorrect results.

### To Reproduce

1. Configure MySQL 5.7+ with `log_output = 'TABLE'` and `general_log = 'ON'`.
2. Run any SQL statement, e.g., `SELECT * FROM information_schema.tables LIMIT 5;`.
3. In OpenMetadata, set up a MySQL ingestion workflow that includes lineage extraction using `mysql.general_log`.
4. Observe that the lineage extraction returns no edges or incomplete lineage.
5. Optionally, query the `general_log` directly in MySQL to confirm the issue:
   ```sql
   SHOW CREATE TABLE mysql.general_log;  -- Shows argument as mediumblob
   SELECT argument FROM mysql.general_log LIMIT 1;  -- Shows binary blob (0x...)

### Expected behavior


---

### 5. Expected behavior（预期行为）⭐ 单独填写

**建议填写**：

```markdown
In MySQL 5.6 and earlier, `argument` is `MEDIUMTEXT`, and OpenMetadata's lineage SQL parser can read it as a normal string, successfully extracting table/column dependencies. The expected behavior is that lineage extraction works on MySQL 5.7+ as well, either by automatically converting the BLOB to TEXT or by handling the field type difference internally.

### OS

windows11

### Python version

_No response_

### OpenMetadata version

1.12.6

### OpenMetadata Ingestion package version

1.12.6

### Additional context

### Additional Context
- MySQL made this change intentionally in version 5.7.3 to avoid character set transformations (release note: [MySQL Bugs #71018](https://bugs.mysql.com/bug.php?id=71018))
- A workaround for end users is to manually convert the BLOB in SQL queries: `CONVERT(argument USING utf8mb4)`, but OpenMetadata's internal lineage extraction should ideally handle this automatically.
- This affects any user who uses MySQL 5.7+ as a source for lineage extraction via the general query log table.

title: ExpressionValidator: regex incorrectly rejects user data inside SpEL string literals

labels.name: java
labels.description: Pull requests that update Java code

labels.name: Need-Discussion
labels.description: Label for when more discussion is needed.

body:
## TL;DR

Our rule validator uses regex to scan SpEL expressions, but regex can't tell the difference between **code** and **data inside string literals**. As a result, legitimate user data — entity names, tag names, FQNs — gets incorrectly rejected when it happens to contain characters like `(`, `Runtime`, or `ClassLoader`.

This is the **same bug class** we just fixed in #27987 (`matchAnyEntityFqn`'s regex), surfacing one layer down. While investigating it, we found several adjacent design questions worth recording. This issue captures the motivation; the team can decide on scope and approach.

---

## What is SpEL? (one-line primer)

SpEL is Spring Expression Language — the syntax users (or our server, on their behalf) write rule conditions in. Examples:

- Alert rule: `matchAnyEntityFqn({'service.db.schema.my_table'})`
- Policy rule: `isOwner() && hasDomain()`

Our validator inspects these strings before they're stored to make sure they're safe to evaluate.

---

## The bug, with a real example

A user creates a Data Quality test suite named `Sales(Q1)2026`. They configure an alert to fire when tests fail. **The alert never fires.**

Step-by-step trace of what happens server-side:

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| 1 | User submits the alert via the UI. The form is structured (dropdowns, value lists). |
| 2 | The server assembles the SpEL rule from the user's input: `matchAnyEntityFqn({'Sales(Q1)2026'})` |
| 3 | The validator scans this text with a regex that looks for **function calls**, defined as the pattern `name(`. |
| 4 | It finds `matchAnyEntityFqn(` — allowed. ✓ |
| 5 | It also finds `Sales(` inside the string literal `'Sales(Q1)2026'` — **not** allowed. ✗ |
| 6 | Validator rejects with: *"Function 'Sales' is not allowed in policy expressions."* |
| 7 | The alert is never created. The user has no idea why. |

The root cause: **the regex doesn't know that text inside `'...'` is data, not code.**

This bites for any FQN, tag, or owner name with `(` in it. Similar misclassifications happen for names containing `Runtime`, `ClassLoader`, `T(...)`, `System.X`, etc. — any token that looks like a dangerous SpEL construct gets flagged even when it's just data.

---

## How we got here

The validator (`ExpressionValidator.validateExpressionSafety`) does two regex scans on the raw expression text:

1. **Dangerous-pattern deny-list** — looks for tokens like `T(`, `new`, `System.`, `Runtime`, `.exec(`, etc. These imply unsafe constructs like `T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec(...)`.
2. **Function-name allow-list** — extracts every `name(` it finds and checks each name against a list of approved functions.

Both scans operate on the *raw text*. Neither understands SpEL's grammar — that single-quoted strings are data, that `''` inside a string is an escaped quote, that `(` inside a string isn't a function call.

This is **the same bug class** as #27987: regex looking at user-controlled text without grammar awareness.

---

## What we found while investigating

Tracing the validator's role through the codebase surfaced several adjacent questions. None of them is customer-blocking today, but they're worth recording so we don't have to re-discover them.

### 1. Spring already blocks the scariest things — natively

Spring's `SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding()` (the evaluation context we already use) refuses to evaluate `T(...)`, `new`, `@beanName`, assignment, or mutation. No code we own is required for those defenses. **The validator's "dangerous patterns" regex is largely duplicating what Spring already does.**

### 2. The validator's *unique* contribution is narrower than it looks

What the validator actually adds beyond Spring's native sandbox:

- **Function allow-list** — only specific methods can be called (`isOwner`, `matchAnyTag`, …). Spring's native sandbox would allow any public method.
- **Property deny-list** — block sensitive getters like `.class`, `.classLoader`. Spring's native sandbox would allow any public property.
- **Submission-time error feedback** — admins find out their rule is bad immediately, not when it tries to evaluate.
- **Future-proofing** — reject any SpEL grammar feature Spring adds later that we haven't reviewed.

That's the real job. The "block dangerous patterns" part overlaps with Spring's own protection.

### 3. Validation runs on every evaluation, not just at submission

Every time a rule is evaluated (e.g., on every entity update for an alert), `CompiledRule.parseExpression` re-runs the validator regex **and** re-parses the SpEL string. For a frequently-firing alert, that's a lot of redundant work — a rule's condition rarely changes after it's stored.

### 4. One code path bypasses the validator entirely

`RBACConditionEvaluator` parses rule conditions with its own SpEL parser and skips the validator. It's safe today (it walks the AST without ever evaluating), but it's a parallel path that doesn't share the validation guarantees.

### 5. Function registration silently fails on OSS deployments

The validator's allow-list of functions is populated by reflecting on a hard-coded list of classes via `Class.forName`. One of those classes only exists in some deployments. When the class isn't on the classpath, `ClassNotFoundException` is silently swallowed and the function set is incomplete — meaning some rules can be incorrectly rejected.

### 6. We've hit this bug class before

#27987 was the same shape one layer up: `matchAnyEntityFqn` did regex matching on FQNs and treated `[TML]` as a regex character class. We shipped the fix. The validator has the same disease in a different place.

---

## Why this issue exists

A single user-visible bug ("my alert isn't firing") expanded, on investigation, into a class of architectural questions about how the validator does its job, where its responsibilities sit relative to Spring's own sandbox, and how it interacts with the rest of the rule-evaluation path.

This issue captures **what we learned**, without prescribing **what to do about it**. The scope of any fix is a separate decision for whoever picks this up:

- The original bug (parentheses in string literals) is well-bounded and could be addressed in isolation.
- The adjacent findings (1–5 above) range from cleanup-flavored to architectural, and may or may not be worth pursuing depending on team priorities.

If a future instance of the same bug class lands, this issue is the breadcrumb trail back to what we already understood.

---
## Solution Design Plan

[PLAN_expression_validator_ast_redesign.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27549037/PLAN_expression_validator_ast_redesign.md)

---

## References

- Customer report (private repo): `open-metadata/openmetadata-collate#4019`
- The fix that shipped for the matching layer: #27987
- Spring SpEL sandboxing primitive: [SimpleEvaluationContext docs](https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/core/expressions/evaluation.html)

title: Datalake connector: JSON columns incorrectly typed as STRING and TypeError logged when ingesting single-object JSON files
body:
## Description

When using the Datalake connector (S3, ADLS, GCS) to ingest single top-level JSON object files, several columns are incorrectly typed as `STRING` and the ingestion logs show repeated `TypeError` messages. Nested field structure is not extracted for the affected columns.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Datalake service (S3, ADLS, or GCS).
2. Upload any single-object JSON file to the configured bucket/prefix — for example a dbt `manifest.json`, `catalog.json`, or any file whose top-level structure is a JSON object (`{ "key": {…}, "key2": {…} }`).
3. Run a metadata ingestion pipeline.
4. Inspect the ingested table's columns in the UI.

## Expected Behavior

- All columns whose values are JSON objects (including empty ones like `{}`) are typed as `JSON` with their nested field structure visible as children in the UI.
- Ingestion logs contain no unexpected errors or warnings.

## Actual Behavior

- Columns whose values are empty JSON objects (`{}`) are typed as `STRING` instead of `JSON`. Their nested structure is not surfaced in the UI.
- The following error appears repeatedly in ingestion logs:

```
TypeError while parsing JSON column children: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not dict. Assuming values are already JSON objects.
```

- The following warning also appears for affected columns:

```
unknown data type object. resolving to string.
```

## Impact

- Users cannot browse nested JSON schema in the UI for affected columns.
- Column-level lineage, tags, and glossary terms cannot be applied to nested fields.
- Repeated error messages make ingestion logs harder to interpret.
- Ingestion of large single-object JSON files takes noticeably longer than expected.

## Environment

- Connector: Datalake (S3 / ADLS / GCS)
- File format: JSON (single top-level object — not an array or JSON Lines)
- Ingestion version: 1.12.x

title: Auto-classification skips 'any'-language recognizers when agent runs with a specific language (e.g. 'en')
body:
### Affected module

Ingestion Framework

### Describe the bug

In `TagAnalyzer.get_recognizers_by()` (`ingestion/src/metadata/pii/tag_analyzer.py`, lines 98–102), when the auto-classification agent runs with a specific language (e.g. `ClassificationLanguage.en`), recognizers whose `supported_language` is `"any"` are silently skipped.

The filter condition is:

```python
if (
    self._language is not ClassificationLanguage.any
    and created.supported_language != self._language.value
):
    continue
```

`"any"` is a valid sentinel meaning "this recognizer works for all languages". When `self._language` is `en`, the condition evaluates `"any" != "en"` → `True` and the recognizer is dropped. This contradicts the intended semantics of the `any` language value.

The same asymmetry does **not** affect the `_analyze_with` method, which already handles the `any` sentinel correctly (lines 142–153): when `self._language is ClassificationLanguage.any` it fans out per-language, but when it is a specific language it calls the analyzer directly — relying on `get_recognizers_by` to have returned the right set. Because `get_recognizers_by` already excluded the `"any"` recognizers, they are never analyzed regardless of direction.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a tag with a recognizer whose `supportedLanguage` is `any` (e.g. a `PatternRecognizer` or `ExactTermsRecognizer`).
2. Configure an auto-classification pipeline agent with `language = en`.
3. Run the pipeline against a table that should match the recognizer.
4. Observe: the tag is **not** applied, even though it should match for all languages.

Minimal Python reproduction:

```python
from metadata.pii.tag_analyzer import TagAnalyzer
from metadata.generated.schema.type.classificationLanguages import ClassificationLanguage

# Assume `tag` has one recognizer with supportedLanguage="any", enabled=True
analyzer = TagAnalyzer(tag=tag, column=col, nlp_engine=nlp, language=ClassificationLanguage.en)
recognizers = analyzer.get_recognizers_by(target=recognizer.Target.column_name)
assert len(recognizers) == 1  # FAILS — returns []
```

### Expected behavior

A recognizer configured with `supportedLanguage = any` should be included when the agent runs with **any** specific language, not just when the agent itself is set to `any`. The filter should be:

```python
if (
    self._language is not ClassificationLanguage.any
    and created.supported_language != self._language.value
    and created.supported_language != ClassificationLanguage.any.value  # ← missing guard
):
    continue
```

### OS

N/A (logic bug, platform-independent)

### Python version

3.11

### OpenMetadata version

main (≥ 1.9.x)

### OpenMetadata Ingestion package version

openmetadata-ingestion (latest main)

### Additional context

- Affected file: `ingestion/src/metadata/pii/tag_analyzer.py`, method `get_recognizers_by`, lines 98–102.
- The `_analyze_with` method (lines 142–153) is **not** affected — its `any`-language branching is correct.
- The fix is a one-line guard; a regression test should assert that `any`-language recognizers are returned when the agent language is a specific value like `en`.

title: Alerting after the Task System Redesign: silent task transitions, unreachable alert configurations, unscoped thread delivery
body:
## Scope

The Task System Redesign (#25894) promoted Task and Announcement to first-class entities and left
Conversation as a `Thread` sub-type, but did not revisit the alerting layer. This epic tracks the
consequences, which fall into three families. Design blueprint:
[ALERTING_AFTER_TASK_REDESIGN.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27528158/ALERTING_AFTER_TASK_REDESIGN.md).

**1. Alerts deliver the wrong things**

- #30555 - entity-scoped filters (FQN, owner, domain, entity id, source) are bypassed for thread events, so an alert scoped to one entity receives conversations about all of them. **Fixed** by #30571. (Thread events reaching entity resources at all is what #28122 and #29112 shipped in 1.12.9 and 1.13; this is the consequence that surfaced.)
- #31330 - `filterByTableNameTestCaseBelongsTo` returns `true` for events it cannot evaluate, the last instance of the pattern behind #30555. Observability-only and narrower on 2.0: incidents now emit `entityType = task`, so only a plain Conversation on a test case reaching a zero-trigger observability `testCase` alert hits it.

**2. Task lifecycle transitions are invisible or misdescribed**

- #29038 - change events are emitted only from the HTTP resource layer, so bulk, incident-driven and workflow-driven transitions stay silent, and there is no `/reopen` endpoint at all.
- #30556 - the resolve/close event that does fire carries a stale `changeDescription` naming workflow-stage fields instead of `status` and `resolution`.
- #29041 - the bulk endpoint emits nothing. **Closed**, subsumed by #29038, whose handler-layer fix covers it; its test criteria moved there.
- #31687 - knowledge page approval tasks are orphaned: `KnowledgePageRepository` still closes and re-assigns through the legacy feed path (two dead `FeedRepository` calls, one of them never even invoked) while every other repository moved to the `TaskRepository` replacements. Standalone bug, and a prerequisite for #30559.
- #31692 - `GlossaryTermRepository.updateTaskWithNewReviewers` is unreachable, so glossary terms have no repository-level approval-task assignee sync; the seeded approval workflow masks it by superseding the task on the next run. Inherited rather than caused by the redesign (already uncalled on 1.13), and the same shape as #31687.

**3. The vocabulary and the descriptors advertise what the backend cannot honor**

- #30557 - nothing declares which event types a resource can emit, and the API validates filter names but never their values. Fix for this and #29040 is in review: #30587 (approved).
- #29040 - the alert builder populates the event-type list from the whole enum regardless of resource.
- #29039 - delete the `EventType` values nothing emits: `taskCreated`, `taskUpdated` and the five `suggestion*` values. No migration needed (subscriptions store event types as plain strings), and the only unparseable historical rows are purged by the seeded retention app. `entityFieldsChanged` is unreachable too but is still used as an internal `PutResponse` marker, so it waits for that refactor; `taskResolved` / `taskClosed` are still emitted and wait for #30559.
- #30558 - `task` exposes only `filterByMentionedName` and `announcement` exposes no filters at all.
- #30559 - retire the legacy thread-task model end to end: close the public feed task API, delete the surface it keeps alive, and remove `taskResolved` / `taskClosed`. Rewritten 2026-08-18; the Recognizer workflow migration it used to wait on already happened, so the remaining blocker is the API decision. Depends on #31687.

Release scope: `TaskResource` and `entity/tasks/task.json` do not exist on 1.13, so every Task-entity
facet above is `main` / 2.0 only. The resource-gate fix (#28122) and its observability guard (#29112)
did reach 1.12.9 and 1.13.

A status pass re-verified against `main` on 2026-07-28 is in
[this comment](https://github.com/open-metadata/OpenMetadata/issues/27889#issuecomment-5101920100).
All code claims were re-verified against `main` (`9ad7ad848e`) on 2026-08-18 and the sub-issues'
line references refreshed.

---

## Origin

Reported by a customer in May 2026: a Notification alert on `glossaryTerm` filtering on
`Thread Created` / `Thread Updated` never fired, with zero entries in *Recent Events* and no error
anywhere. That specific case was fixed by #28122 and shipped in 1.12.9 and 1.13. Investigating it
surfaced the rest of the drift tracked above.

Internal discussion: https://collate-inc.slack.com/archives/C096NDJQAJW/p1777900803665159

title: OMjob operator tolerations are not working in scheduled jobs
body: ### Affected module Backend ### Describe the bug After upgrading to 1.12.6 and redeploying all the pipeline jobs, scheduled pipelines fail. The scheduled run creates a pod with the correct image and nodeselector, but without the configured tolerations. As a result, pods remain Pending on tainted nodes. but manual pipeline runs work correctly: the generated OMJob includes the configured nodeselector and tolerations, and the resulting pod schedules successfully. I verified both the CRD'S omjobs and cronomjobs reflect the new toleration field What is more critical is removing toleration or nodeselector from values does not remove it from the newly scheduled pods, even after redeployment of all pipelines. ### To Reproduce 1. Add a toleration field in the helm values 2. Redeploy a scheduled job pipeline 3. Once the job runs, inspect the manifest to see the absent added toleration 4. Revert the toleration by removing the toleration field 5. Redeploy pipelines 6. The newly created jobs from scheduled jobs will still have the toleration field. ### Expected behavior 1. Tolerations present on the scheduled omjobs 2. Removing toleration or nodeselector reflect change on the newly creaed omjobs(with or without redeployment) ### OS Amazon linux 2023 ### Python version _No response_ ### OpenMetadata version 1.12.6 ### OpenMetadata Ingestion package version _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ ### Pre-submission checklist - [x] I searched for duplicate issues. - [x] I removed credentials, hostnames, emails, and other sensitive data from logs and config.

### Affected module

Ingestion Framework

### Describe the bug

In OpenMetadata 1.12.x, Unity Catalog ingestion fails when httpPath is not provided in the connection configuration. Although httpPath is optional in the schema/UI, ingestion crashes due to improper initialization of connectionArguments.

This issue is a regression bug.

2. Run metadata ingestion/Test Connection.

title: Product tour badge intermittently missing on /tour page load
body:
## Description
The product tour intermittently fails to start on the /tour page, especially in slower AUT runs or after directly reloading /tour.

The page content renders successfully, including the activity feed widget, but the tour overlay/badge ([data-tour-elem="badge"]) is not visible. In some manual cases, the tour briefly appears for a few milliseconds and then disappears.

### Steps To Reproduce

- Log in to OpenMetadata.
- Navigate to /tour directly, or open the tour from the Help menu.
- Reload /tour, or run the Playwright tour flow in a slower/AUT environment.
- Wait for the page content to render.

### Actual Behavior
The tour badge is sometimes missing, and the tour does not start. Playwright fails while waiting for: `[data-tour-elem="badge"]`

### Expected Behavior
The tour should reliably start once the first tour target is rendered, and the badge should remain visible at step

title: Inconsistent validation for Custom Property names causes search failures with special characters
body:
**Affected module**
Does it impact the UI, backend or Ingestion Framework?
UI, Backend

**Describe the bug**
Creating of Custom Property allow special characters in customProperty Name, via API/ingestion but were previously restricted in UI. Recent changes removed UI validation, allowing invalid CP names that break search.

- UI now allows  customProperty names with special characters (e.g. pw._CP-ccaa2136.dashboard:/&^%$#@!)
- Backend has no validation, so API/ingestion also accepts them
- These names are used as keys in multiple places (ES, JSON paths, FQN, etc.)

**To Reproduce**

Screenshots or steps to reproduce

**Expected behavior**
Consistent validation across UI, backend, and ingestion
CP names should only allow safe characters

**Version:**
 - OpenMetadata version: 1.12.6

**Proposed Fix**

- Restore strict validation in UI (allow limited safe pattern, e.g. ^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9.]*$ if dots are required)
- Add same validation in backend (customProperty.json / API layer)
- Ensure ingestion respects the same constraints
- Update help text to match actual validation

title: Empty allowedEmailRegistrationDomains blocks all OAuth self-signups
body:
## Description

After PR #25391 introduced domain validation in the OAuth self-signup flow, an empty `allowedEmailRegistrationDomains` array (`[]`) blocks **all** new user registrations via OAuth instead of allowing them.

## Root Cause

The domain check in `AuthenticationCodeFlowHandler.getOrCreateOidcUser()` (line 932) does not account for an empty set:

```java
Set<String> allowedDomains = authorizerConfiguration.getAllowedEmailRegistrationDomains();
if (allowedDomains != null
    && !allowedDomains.contains("all")
    && !allowedDomains.contains(domain)) {
  throw new AuthenticationException("Email domain not allowed for self-signup: " + domain);
}
```

An empty `Set` is not `null`, doesn't contain `"all"`, and doesn't contain any domain — so **every** signup is rejected.

The JSON schema defaults this field to `[]`, meaning any deployment that didn't explicitly configure it now silently blocks all OAuth self-registrations.

## Impact

- **Regression** from prior behavior where empty `[]` meant "no domain restrictions"
- Since 1.12, this field is **no longer exposed in the UI** (removed due to user confusion with `principalDomain` and `allowedDomains`), making it impossible to fix without a direct API call to `PATCH /api/v1/system/security/config`
- Any customer upgrading to a version with this change will have broken OAuth self-signup if `allowedEmailRegistrationDomains` was left at the default

## Error Log

```
WARN SECURITY: Blocked OAuth signup for disallowed domain: gmail.com (user: user@gmail.com)
```

## Fix

Add `!allowedDomains.isEmpty()` to the condition to restore backwards-compatible behavior:

```java
if (allowedDomains != null
    && !allowedDomains.isEmpty()       // treat empty as "no restrictions"
    && !allowedDomains.contains("all")
    && !allowedDomains.contains(domain)) {
```

## Release

1.12.5

title: [BUG] S3 Ingestion Failure: Pydantic ValidationError 'extra_forbidden' for BucketArn in S3BucketResponse
body:
**Affected module**
Ingestion Framework (S3 Storage Connector)
**Bug Description**
The S3 ingestion fails during the metadata extraction phase due to a Pydantic validation error. The S3BucketResponse model in the ingestion framework is configured to forbid extra fields. When AWS returns the **BucketArn** field—which appears to be included in recent Boto3/S3 API responses—the ingestion process crashes with a pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: Extra inputs are not permitted.
**_To Reproduce_**
Configure an S3 Storage Service in OpenMetadata 1.12.4.
Run a Metadata Ingestion pipeline using the Kubernetes Executor.
The logs will show the connection test passing (ListBuckets and GetMetrics are successful).
As soon as the topology_runner starts fetching bucket details, the process fails with the following traceback:
`pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for S3BucketResponse
BucketArn
  Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden, input_value='arn:aws:s3:::bucket-nameXXXX', input_type=str]`

**Expected behavior**
The ingestion should successfully list and ingest S3 buckets even if the AWS API returns additional fields like BucketArn. The Pydantic model should allow extra fields (extra='allow') or explicitly include BucketArn to maintain backward and forward compatibility with AWS API updates.
**Version:**
OS: Kubernetes Executor
Python version: 3.10.20
OpenMetadata version: 1.12.4
OpenMetadata Ingestion package version: openmetadata-ingestion[s3]==1.12.4.1
**Additional context**
The error seems tied to the migration to Pydantic V2 in the 1.12.x branch. Because the Kubernetes Executor uses the openmetadata/ingestion:1.12.4 image, the strict validation settings in metadata/ingestion/source/storage/s3/models.py (or the corresponding S3 source file) prevent the ingestion of any bucket that returns more metadata than strictly defined in the OpenMetadata schema.

title: Race condition in ActivityFeedPublisher and WorkflowEventConsumer when entity is deleted shortly after creation
body:
**Affected module**
Does it impact the UI, backend or Ingestion Framework?
Backend

**Describe the bug**
When an entity (e.g., a table) is created and then deleted in quick succession via the REST API, the `ActivityFeedPublisher` and `WorkflowEventConsumer` throw errors. These async consumers attempt to fetch the entity from the database to generate activity feeds and workflow entity links, but the entity has already been deleted by the time they execute.
This is a race condition between the synchronous API response path (which completes the delete) and the asynchronous event consumers (which still reference the entity by ID from the original create event).

**To Reproduce**

1. Create an entity via the REST API (e.g., `PUT /api/v1/tables`).
2. Immediately delete the same entity via the REST API (e.g., `DELETE /api/v1/tables/{id}`).
3. Observe errors in the server logs from ActivityFeedPublisher and WorkflowEventConsumer.

Note: If a delay is introduced between steps 1 and 2 (allowing the async consumers to finish processing the create event), the error does not occur.


**Expected behavior**
The platform should handle rapid create → delete sequences gracefully. The async event consumers should either:

- Carry the entity snapshot/payload within the event itself, eliminating the need for a DB round-trip, or
- Catch EntityNotFoundException when the entity no longer exists and silently acknowledge/skip the event without logging an error.

**Current Behavior**
ActivityFeedPublisher and WorkflowEventConsumer throw EntityNotFoundException (or equivalent) because the entity has been deleted from the database before the consumers could process the create event.

[splunk-query.csv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26176232/splunk-query.csv)

**Use Case / Impact**
This issue impacts event-driven metadata ingestion workflows. In environments where metadata changes (e.g., AWS Glue table change events) are captured and pushed to OpenMetadata via the REST API in real time, the system does not control the timing or order of events. Ephemeral/temporary tables that are created and dropped rapidly are a normal occurrence in data platforms, and the current behavior causes persistent error noise in logs and potential event processing failures.
This is distinct from batch ingestion (scheduled jobs), where the time between operations is typically long enough for async consumers to complete.

The request succeeds but parsing fails in:

```

dict(bool)

RCA:
The issue appears to be caused by a mismatch between the OpenAPI schema and the actual API response.

In the response payload:
change_description.fields_updated[].old_value = bool

However the generated model expects old_value to be a dict/object, causing:
dict(bool)
which triggers the exception.

**Expected behavior**
A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.

**Additional context**
Update the OpenAPI schema for:
changeDescription.fieldsUpdated[].oldValue
to allow multiple types (e.g. object | boolean) or ensure the API always returns a consistent structure.

[OSS Thread reference](https://openmetadata.slack.com/archives/C02B6955S4S/p1773329878303149)

title: BigQuery Profiler Failure

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
**Affected module**
Profiler

**Describe the bug**
Profiler column query metrics failing when column names are not lowercase.

```python
  File "profiler_interface.py", line 270, in _compute_query_metrics
      sample.__table__.c[column.name]
  File "sqlalchemy/sql/base.py", line 1214, in __getitem__
      return self._index[key]
  KeyError: 'reservationId'
```

**To Reproduce**
Create a BigQuery table with columns that are not lowercase and run the profiler.

**Expected behavior**
Profiler should just work

**Version:**
 - OpenMetadata version: 1.11.3

**Additional context**
Small analysis:

Root Cause: Column Name vs. Column Key Mismatch

The bug is a case sensitivity mismatch between two identifiers for the same column.

Step 1 — ORM column creation (ingestion/src/metadata/profiler/orm/converter/base.py:88-98):

```python
  return sqlalchemy.Column(
      name=str(col.name.root),          # "reservationId"  (original case from OM metadata)
      ...
      key=str(col.name.root).lower(),   # "reservationid"  (forced lowercase)
  )
```
The .key is lowercased — this was added as a Snowflake case-sensitivity fix. However, it has a side effect: SQLAlchemy indexes the .c collection by .key, not .name.

Step 2 — Profiler tries to access the column (profiler_interface.py:269-272):

```python
  sample_column = (
      sample.__table__.c[column.name]      # Lookups by .name = "reservationId"
      if hasattr(sample, "__table__")
      else sample.c[column.name]
  )
```
This uses column.name ("reservationId") to index into .c, but .c is keyed by .key ("reservationid"). KeyError.

The Fix
In profiler_interface.py:270-272, use column.key instead of column.name:

```python
  sample_column = (
      sample.__table__.c[column.key]       # ← use .key to match SQLAlchemy's index
      if hasattr(sample, "__table__")
      else sample.c[column.key]
  )
```

GET_DDL() queries fail for Snowflake tables with dots in their names.

## Expected Behavior
Tables with names like `CDB_LU_AP.DSPA_ADDRESSES_INITIAL_LOAD` should have their DDL fetched and schemaDefinition populated.

## Actual Behavior
GET_DDL() calls fail with error 002003 "Database does not exist or not authorized"

## Root Cause
Unquoted identifiers are parsed by Snowflake, treating dots as separators. 
The fix: quote all identifiers when building GET_DDL() calls.

## Impact
Tables with lowercase and special characters like '.' in their names do not get their DDL in Openmetadata.

title: Databricks ingestion extremely slow due to unbounded pipeline status extraction
body:
**Affected module**
Does it impact the UI, backend or Ingestion Framework? - Ingestion

**Describe the bug**
A clear and concise description of what the bug is.
- We are observing very long runtimes for Databricks ingestion pipeline After investigation, the main bottleneck is pipeline status ingestion.

body: **Affected module** This may only affect Unity Catalog data assets, but it could also affect other databases. **Affected module**
Backend 


**Describe the bug**
On OM 1.10.14 on Kubernetes (with multiple pods)

```
 curl -v -H "Proxy-Authorization: Bearer $IAP_BEARER" -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" -H 'Content-Type: application/json-patch+json' -X PATCH "$OM_BASE_URL/api/v1/databases/57dd8e35-4c7a-4409-a609-b4a9203a6723" -d '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/extension/dialect", "value": "xxxxx"}]'| jq .

this **succeeds only 25%** of the times I try (on the same entity). 

Usually I get 
```
 curl -v -H "Proxy-Authorization: Bearer $IAP_BEARER" -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" -H 'Content-Type: application/json-patch+json' -X PATCH "$OM_BASE_URL/api/v1/databases/57dd8e35-4c7a-4409-a609-b4a9203a6723" -d '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/extension/dialect", "value": "xxxxx"}]'| jq .

## Issue Description
There is a discrepancy in the `tableRowInsertedCountToBeBetween` test definition when using PostgreSQL with the Collate-based version.

### Current Behavior (Incorrect - PostgreSQL Collate)

- `columnName` (required)
- `rangeType` (required)
- `rangeInterval` (required)

```json
{
  "id": "fef3f0a3-5230-4e2d-9091-7967c3e09ca7",
  "name": "tableRowInsertedCountToBeBetween",
  "parameterDefinition": [
    {
      "name": "min",

      "dataType": "INT",
      "description": "Lower Bound of the Count",
      "required": false
    },
    {
      "name": "max",
      "displayName": "Max Row Count",
      "dataType": "INT",
      "description": "Upper Bound of the Count",
      "required": false
    }
  ]
}
```

### Expected Behavior (Correct)
The test definition should include all five parameters:

```json
{
  "id": "642880f2-f425-4cdd-8de5-d5e41d7c0039",
  "name": "tableRowInsertedCountToBeBetween",
  "parameterDefinition": [
    {
      "name": "min",
      "displayName": "Min Row Count",
      "dataType": "INT",
      "description": "Lower Bound of the Count",
      "required": false
    },
    {
      "name": "max",
      "displayName": "Max Row Count",
      "dataType": "INT",
      "description": "Upper Bound of the Count",
      "required": false
    },
    {
      "name": "columnName",
      "displayName": "Column Name",
      "dataType": "STRING",
      "description": "Name of the Column. It should be a timestamp, date or datetime field.",
      "required": true
    },
    {
      "name": "rangeType",
      "displayName": "Range Type",
      "dataType": "STRING",
      "description": "One of 'HOUR', 'DAY', 'MONTH', 'YEAR'",
      "required": true
    },
    {
      "name": "rangeInterval",
      "displayName": "Interval",
      "dataType": "INT",
      "description": "Interval Range. E.g. if rangeInterval=1 and rangeType=DAY, we'll check the numbers of rows inserted where columnName=-1 DAY",
      "required": true
    }
  ]
}
```

### Environment Details
- **Works correctly**: OSS (MySQL + PostgreSQL), Collate (MySQL)
- **Broken**: Collate with PostgreSQL

### Steps to Reproduce

4. Observe missing `columnName`, `rangeType`, and `rangeInterval` parameters

title: KafkaConnect → S3 lineage skipped due to incomplete container_name resolution
body:
**Affected module**
Does it impact the UI, backend or Ingestion Framework?
Ingestion

**Describe the bug**
I’m trying to set up lineage for the following pipeline:

Kafka → KafkaConnect → S3
using the KafkaConnect connector, but lineage is not being created for the S3 target.
After debugging the code, it appears that KafkaConnectDatasetDetails.container_name is not being populated correctly, which causes the storage entity FQN resolution to fail and the lineage to be skipped entirely.

While digging through the code, I found the following behavior:

`KafkaConnectDatasetDetails.container_name` is populated by `get_connector_dataset_info`
This method derives the value from topics.dir
However, topics.dir only contains the directory path inside the bucket, not the full storage container name
As a result, container_name is set to only the prefix instead of the full bucket/container name.

Example
```
KafkaConnectDatasetDetails(
  table=None,
  database=None,
  container_name='raw_kafka',
  column_mappings=[]
)
```
This value is later used to build the StorageContainer FQN, but since it is incomplete, the FQN resolution returns None, causing the lineage to be skipped silently.

----

I found that for Kafka connectors to Iceberg, we can easily extract the table name from the following entry:
`"iceberg.tables": "table"`
For the Kafka Connector to BigQuery, here are the tests we've performed:
Working Addition:
```
database.server.name = "database"
table.include.list = table1
```
Not Working:
```
database.server.name = "database"
table.include.list = table1, table2
```

**To Reproduce**

Screenshots or steps to reproduce

**Expected behavior**

- container_name should resolve to the actual storage container/bucket name (e.g., full S3 bucket name)
- Storage entity FQN should be constructed correctly
- Lineage between KafkaConnect and S3 should be created

**Version:**
 - OS: [e.g. iOS]

The core REST client (metadata/ingestion/ometa/client.py) incorrectly handles successful API responses (HTTP 200/201) that contain non-JSON bodies (e.g., text/plain).
When resp.json() fails because the response body is a raw string (like a JWT token), the code falls into a catch-all except Exception block. This block logs a warning but fails to return the response object. Consequently, the method returns None by default. This leads to an AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'text' in the calling module (e.g., the NiFi connector) when it tries to access the raw body via res.text.

**To Reproduce**

- Configure any connector or service that returns a raw string in a successful response (Example: NiFi's /nifi-api/access/token endpoint which returns a raw JWT string with Content-Type: text/plain).
- Run the ingestion.
- Observe the logs: WARNING - Unexpected error while returning response <Response [201]> in json format - Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0). Followed by: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'text' in nifi/client.py.

**Expected behavior**
The _one_request method should be resilient to non-JSON payloads. If resp.json() fails but the request was successful, it should return the raw resp (Response) object so that the specific connector can decide how to handle the data.

**Version:**
 - OS: Linux / Docker (Windows Host)
 - Python version: 3.10
 - OpenMetadata version: 1.10.10
 - OpenMetadata Ingestion package version: docker.getcollate.io/openmetadata/ingestion:1.10.10

**Additional context**
The fix involves ensuring that the Response object is returned even when JSON decoding fails.

Current problematic code in ometa/client.py:
```
except Exception as exc:
    logger.debug(traceback.format_exc())
    logger.warning(
        f"Unexpected error while returning response {resp} in json format - {exc}"
    )
    # The function ends here and returns None implicitly
```
Proposed Fix:
```
except Exception as exc:
    logger.debug(traceback.format_exc())
    logger.warning(
        f"Unexpected error while returning response {resp} in json format - {exc}"
    )
    return resp
```

This fix was tested locally by patching the file inside the ingestion container. It successfully allowed the NiFi connector to retrieve the Bearer Token and proceed with metadata extraction.

title: Notifications Missing Global Recipient Deduplication
body:
#### **Problem**

When an `EventSubscription` includes multiple destinations that resolve to overlapping recipients, users receive duplicate notifications. Each destination is processed independently, so recipients appearing in more than one destination get the same notification multiple times.

**Example:**

* Destination 1: Email + Owners → `owner@example.com`
* Destination 2: Email + Mentions → `{owner@example.com, other@example.com}`
  **Result:** `owner@example.com` receives **two** identical emails.

#### **Root Cause**

There is **no global recipient deduplication** across destinations.
Each destination resolves recipients separately, and internal deduplication only occurs *within* a single destination. No mechanism tracks recipients already notified during the same event cycle.

**Key Flow:**

* `createEventsWithReceivers()` attaches all destination IDs to each event
* `publishEvents()` iterates destinations sequentially
* Each publisher (`EmailPublisher`, `SlackPublisher`, etc.) resolves recipients independently
* `RecipientResolver` returns a per-destination recipient set, unaware of other destinations
* No cross-destination deduplication is performed

#### **Relevant Code**

* `AbstractEventConsumer.java` (307–315): `createEventsWithReceivers()`
* `AbstractEventConsumer.java` (195–205): `publishEvents()`
* `EmailPublisher`, `SlackEventPublisher`, etc.: Per-destination recipient resolution
* `RecipientResolver.java`: Independent recipient sets per destination

#### **Impact**

* Users receive duplicate notifications when multiple destinations overlap
* Affects Email, Slack, MS Teams, GChat, Webhooks
* Occurs when the same transport type is used in multiple destinations

title: Trino connector: incorrect handling of SSL verify parameter - passing dict instead of path or False
body: In the Trino connector implementation, the SSL verify parameter is being handled incorrectly. in the file https://github.com/open-metadata/OpenMetadata/blob/d8ac493d11f0606f8f40b22cbdd416b1975524f8/ingestion/src/metadata/ingestion/source/database/trino/connection.py#L219 the code assigns a dict to verify, but this parameter should accept either: a boolean (True/False), or a path to a CA certificate file (string) Passing a dict breaks the expected behavior of the underlying HTTP client used for Trino connections. ### How to reproduce Configure a Trino ingestion connection over HTTPS. Provide a custom CA certificate path or set verify: false in the connection configuration. The ingestion process either fails during connection or does not correctly apply the SSL verification options, because the code transforms verify into a dict instead of using the actual provided value. ### Expected behavior When verify is set to a file path, the Trino connection should use that CA certificate. When verify is set to False, SSL verification should be disabled. The connector should pass the value directly to the underlying HTTP library, which follows the standard requests semantics (verify accepts True, False, or a path string). ### Proposed fix Replace the current logic (which constructs a dict for verify) with a direct assignment: - connection_args.root['verify'] = { ... } # currently creates a dict (incorrect) + connection_args.root['verify'] = connection.verify # correctly accepts path or False This ensures that the connector behaves consistently with Python’s standard SSL verification handling. ### Why this matters Enables proper use of custom CA certificates (enterprise/internal PKI). Allows disabling SSL verification when required for testing or controlled environments. Restores compatibility with how the underlying HTTP libraries expect the verify parameter.

title: Bug: Okta SSO validation in UI incorrectly requires /v1/keys endpoint, fails for /oauth2/v1/keys in v1.10.6
body:
Overview
Version: OpenMetadata 1.10.6

When attempting to update Okta SSO settings in the UI (e.g., to change domains), a validation error occurs. The validation logic incorrectly assumes the Okta JWKS endpoint must be at /v1/keys.

This fails for any Okta organization that uses the standard /oauth2/v1/keys endpoint for their authorization server.

The Error
When saving the configuration via the UI (PATCH /api/v1/system/security/config), the following error is logged:

ERROR [2025-11-13 03:05:42,891] [dw-147 - PATCH /api/v1/system/security/config] o.o.s.r.s.SystemResource - Security configuration validation failed: authenticationConfiguration.publicKeyUrls: Public key URL validation failed: At least one public key URL must be the Okta JWKS endpoint: https://xxxxxxxxxx.okta.com/v1/keys
Problem Details
The root cause is that our Okta public keys are located at https://[my-okta-domain].okta.com/oauth2/v1/keys. The UI validation logic seems to be hardcoded to check only for .../v1/keys and fails the update.

This configuration worked correctly in version 1.9.x and continues to work in 1.10.x if it was configured via environment variables and the UI security page is not touched. The moment an admin tries to modify the settings in the UI, this validation bug prevents any changes.

Working Configuration (via Environment Variables)
This is the configuration that was previously working and which we are trying to replicate in the UI:

# Authentication provider settings
AUTHENTICATION_PROVIDER=okta
AUTHENTICATION_CLIENT_ID=REDACTED
AUTHENTICATION_PUBLIC_KEYS=[https://[my-okta-domain].okta.com/oauth2/v1/keys, https://[my-openmetadata-domain]/api/v1/system/config/jwks]  
AUTHENTICATION_AUTHORITY=https://[my-okta-domain].okta.com/
AUTHENTICATION_CALLBACK_URL=http://[my-openmetadata-domain]/callback

# OIDC settings
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=REDACTED
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=REDACTED
OIDC_DISCOVERY_URI=https://[my-okta-domain].okta.com/.well-known/openid-configuration 
OIDC_CALLBACK=http://[my-openmetadata-domain]/callback


https://openmetadata.slack.com/archives/C02B6955S4S/p1763003376008879

title: Duplicate tags in ChangeEvent notifications for Entity tag updates
body:
# **Affected module**

**Backend**

## **Describe the bug**

ChangeEvent notifications for table column tag updates report duplicate tags in the ChangeDescription. When updating tags on a table column, the `fieldsAdded` array
contains duplicate entries of the same tag, even though the entity itself stores only one instance.

## **To Reproduce**

1. Update tags on a table column (e.g., change from `PII.Sensitive` to `PII.None`)
2. Observe the ChangeDescription in the generated ChangeEvent
3. The `fieldsAdded` array shows duplicate tag entries:

```plaintext
fieldsAdded=[
  FieldChange[name=columns.xxx.tags, newValue=[
    {"tagFQN":"PII.None","name":"None",...},
    {"tagFQN":"PII.None","name":"None",...}  // duplicate
  ]]
]
```

## **Expected behavior**

Each tag should appear only once in the ChangeDescription `fieldsAdded` array, matching the actual entity state.

## **Root cause**

`EntityRepository.updateTags()` (line 4020-4067) pre-calculates `addedTags` and `deletedTags`, then passes these pre-populated lists to `recordListChange()`.
However, `recordListChange()` is designed to calculate diffs itself by adding to the provided lists, causing duplicates.
Other implementations like `GlossaryTermRepository` correctly pass empty lists to `recordListChange()`.

## **Version**
* **OpenMetadata version:** main branch

Open the Permission Evaluator for that table and evaluate the rule. 6. Observe the condition evaluates to False and access is denied. **Screenshots** **Expected behavior** Conditions should evaluate to True for tables that carry the ingested label om_layer:l1 (displayed as a tag in OM), so the rule can match accordingly. **Version:** - OS: : kubernetes , ubuntu - Python version:3.10 - OpenMetadata version: 1.9.7 - OpenMetadata Ingestion package version: [e.g. `openmetadata-ingestion[docker]==1.9.7 `] - Source: BigQuery connector **Additional context** - In BigQuery parlance “tag” can refer to policy tags; here we are using labels. These labels ingest and appear in OM as tags on the table, and are visible in the Classification tab. - Issue persists after upgrading from 1.9.1 to 1.9.7. - Goal is to rely on ingested tags from source systems (avoid manual tag creation in OM) to provide conditional access to resources.

title: Postgres pg_stat_statements Compatibility Issue with GetQueries on Postgres 13+
body:
**Affected module**
Does it impact the UI, backend or Ingestion Framework? -- ingestion

**Describe the bug**
A clear and concise description of what the bug is.
- We’ve encountered an issue with the OpenMetadata GetQueries logic when connected to a PostgreSQL database running version 13 or later. The error occurs because the underlying query references a column that no longer exists in newer versions of PostgreSQL.

```
(psycopg2.errors.UndefinedColumn) column s.total_exec_time does not exist
LINE 7:         s.total_exec_time duration
                ^
[SQL: /* {"app": "OpenMetadata", "version": "1.7.2.1"} */
      SELECT
        u.usename,
        d.datname database_name,
        s.query query_text,
        s.total_exec_time duration
      FROM
        pg_stat_statements s
        JOIN pg_catalog.pg_database d ON s.dbid = d.oid
        JOIN pg_catalog.pg_user u ON s.userid = u.usesysid
]
```
In PostgreSQL 13 and later, the column total_exec_time in pg_stat_statements was renamed to total_time.

**To Reproduce**

Screenshots or steps to reproduce

A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.

pipeline_request = CreatePipelineRequest(

title: Don't store `null` secrets in Secrets Manager
body:
Using the OM server configured with `managed-aws`:

process:
1. create snowflake service with a password & passKey
2. edit snowflake service, make changes in the password field and then remove them
3. save

Using external dashboards to enrich or reinterpret DAG run metadata for better clarity. **Additional context** Having consistent and accurate time representations is essential for debugging, auditing, and communicating ingestion timings, especially in distributed teams.

title: Superset ingestion uses bad query
body:
**Affected module**
Ingestion Framework

**Describe the bug**
Superset ingestion uses the following query:
```
select 
	tc.id, 
    	tc.table_name ,
    	tc.column_name, 
		tc.table_id, 
    	tc.type,
    	tc.description 
from 
	table_columns  tc  
inner join 
	tables t 
on 
	t.id=tc.table_id  
where 
	tc.table_id=%(table_id)s
```
It's trying to select tc.table_name but the column table_name is not in the table table_columns but in the table tables. So I think the query should be 

```
select 
	tc.id, 
    	t.table_name ,
    	tc.column_name, 
		tc.table_id, 
    	tc.type,
    	tc.description 
from 
	table_columns  tc  
inner join 
	tables t 
on 
	t.id=tc.table_id  
where 
	tc.table_id=%(table_id)s
```
I also think this is the reason why the ingestion for superset is always in `running` state

**To Reproduce**

To reproduce this error you can simply run the first query on your superset postgres database and then try the second one and you should see that the query will run the second time.

**Expected behavior**
A running query that does not populate ingestion logs with errors

**Version:**
 - OS: [e.g. iOS]
 - Python version:
 - OpenMetadata version: 1.7
 - OpenMetadata Ingestion package version: Im using the UI but my openmetadata ingestion version is also 1.7

title: Oracle lineage ingestion fails due to an error ORA-00933: SQL command not properly ended
body:
**Affected module**
Impacts Ingestion Framework (lineage build feature).

**Describe the bug**
Faced with failures during lineage ingestion from an Oracle RDBMS source in OpenMetadata.
The issues are related to SQL parsing errors and entity handling:
1. Query History Parsing Error (ORA-00933)
The following query on gv$sql fails:
> ORA-00933: SQL command not properly ended

Something with LIKE conditions, such as:
`SQL_FULLTEXT NOT LIKE '/* {"app": "OpenMetadata", %%} */%%'`
But i can launch it with SQL Developer and got some results:
![SQLDev](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc2ee26d-f043-4561-bf23-706545fe833e)

There are another set of errors and warnings, like:
2. SQL Parsing Failure on CREATE VIEW statements
The ingestion fails to parse "CREATE OR REPLACE FORCE VIEW ... AS SELECT ... WITH READ ONLY" queries.
> ingesting lineage failed: An Identifier is expected, got Token[value: (] instead.

For example: DBA$OLAP_DIM_LEVEL_ATTRIBUTES

3. Stored Procedure Lineage Ingestion Conflict
> api request failure: Entity already exists

I think this occurs when a procedure or its lineage was previously ingested.
It seems there is not "retry" or "update" feature (or i can't see it, maybe it is an incremental mechanism?).

But the main root cause of not getting lineage for objects in №1.
I've tried several times - with creating a new user and granting rights only to needed schema and with giving a full SYSDBA access to OpenMetadata while creating ingestions.

**To Reproduce**
1) Create user and give access as per [documentation](https://docs.open-metadata.org/latest/connectors/database/oracle)
```sql
CREATE USER openmetadataoracle IDENTIFIED by openmetadataoracle;
GRANT CREATE SESSION TO openmetadataoracle;
GRANT SELECT_CATALOG_ROLE to openmetadataoracle;
--GRANT SELECT ANY TABLE TO openmetadataoracle;
--REVOKE SELECT ANY TABLE FROM openmetadataoracle;
BEGIN
  FOR t IN (
    SELECT table_name FROM all_tables WHERE owner = 'PLN_MRPS'
  ) LOOP
    EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'GRANT SELECT ON DB_TEST_SCHEMA.' || t.table_name || ' TO openmetadataoracle';
  END LOOP;
END;
/
```
In this schema (Oracle Hyperion Planning application) there are no connected columns, so OpenMetadata should build it with lineage feature by itself.
2) Add ingestion to metadata, launch it (i have a partial success)
3) Add lineage ingestion, launch it (failed)
![Statuses](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5fe7af49-6387-4212-8ee7-0493b3992784)

**Expected behavior**
Success of partial success status for lineage.
All parsed objects with history from v$sql are connected.

**Version:**
 - OS: Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS
 - Python version: 3.10.12
 - OpenMetadata version: 1.6.6
 - OpenMetadata Ingestion package version: 1.6.6

**Additional context**
Logs:
[Oracle_SYS_lineage_1.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19973849/Oracle_SYS_lineage_1.log)
[Oracle_Schema_lineage_2.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19973851/Oracle_Schema_lineage_2.log)

title: S3 storage metadata ingestion only processes 5 containers
body:
**Affected module**
Ingestion Framework

**Describe the bug**
I'm running OpenMetadata 1.6.3 locally and testing ingestion from an S3 bucket with about 30 folders of JSON ETLs from a database.

The structure of the bucket is:

```text
openmetadata.json
21.04/output/etl/json/table1/{...json files}
21.04/output/etl/json/table2/{...json files}
...
21.04/output/etl/json/table30/{...json files}
```

The contents of the `openmetadata.json` file at the root of the bucket are:

```json
{
    "entries": [
        {
            "dataPath": "21.04/output/etl/json",
            "structureFormat": "json",
            "isPartitioned": false,
            "depth": 1
        }
    ]
}
```

The ingestion log only processes 5 of the subfolders at the prefix specified at dataPath:

```text
[2025-03-03T21:04:53.337+0000] {logger.py:192} INFO - Workflow OpenMetadata Summary:
[2025-03-03T21:04:53.337+0000] {logger.py:192} INFO - Processed records: 5
[2025-03-03T21:04:53.337+0000] {logger.py:192} INFO - Updated records: 0
[2025-03-03T21:04:53.337+0000] {logger.py:192} INFO - Warnings: 0
[2025-03-03T21:04:53.337+0000] {logger.py:192} INFO - Errors: 0
[2025-03-03T21:04:53.337+0000] {logger.py:192} INFO - Success %: 100.0
```

**To Reproduce**

Screenshots or steps to reproduce

1. Deploy the containerized OpenMetadata 1.6.3 locally
2. Create an S3 storage service
3. Create an ingestion for the S3 storage service with no Include or Exclude filters
4. Run the ingestion

The dataset I am using is a copy of the following:
https://platform.opentargets.org/downloads


**Expected behavior**
I have more than 5 tables ingested. The metadata ingestion processes all (30) folders under the specified `dataPath` and `depth`. Errors with processing tables are captured and reported in the summary.

**Version:**
 - OS: macOS
 - Python version: whatever is available in the `openmetadata/server:1.6.3` container image
 - OpenMetadata version: 1.6.3
 - OpenMetadata Ingestion package version: `openmetadata-ingestion[docker]==1.6.3`

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.

In initial inspection, there was an error processing a `_SUCCESS` status flag file in the ingestion log, but this had no bearing on the outcome. Adding an exclusion filter seemed to avoid touching these files, but the outcome was the same - only 5 containers/tables were processed out of 30.

title: Auto Classification Ingestion fails for Databricks Unity
body: **Affected module** Does it impact the UI, backend or Ingestion Framework? The defect affects the Ingestion Framework, specifically the process from Databricks Unity. **Describe the bug** I am trying to run Auto Classification Ingestion on Databricks Unity; however, it constantly fails with the following error: ``` ... AttributeError: 'WorkspaceClient' object has no attribute 'connect' [2025-02-05T10:17:08.712+0000] {sampler_interface.py:250} WARNING - Error fetching sample data: 'WorkspaceClient' object has no attribute 'connect' [2025-02-05T10:17:08.715+0000] {status.py:91} WARNING - Unexpected exception processing entity Unity.X.Y.Z: 'WorkspaceClient' object has no attribute 'connect' [2025-02-05T10:17:08.715+0000] {status.py:92} DEBUG - Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/airflow/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/metadata/sampler/sqlalchemy/sampler.py", line 186, in fetch_sample_data .all() File "/home/airflow/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/query.py", line 2773, in all return self._iter().all() File "/home/airflow/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/query.py", line 2916, in _iter result = self.session.execute( File "/home/airflow/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/session.py", line 1716, in execute conn = self._connection_for_bind(bind) File "/home/airflow/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/session.py", line 1555, in _connection_for_bind return self._transaction._connection_for_bind( File "/home/airflow/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/session.py", line 750, in _connection_for_bind conn = bind.connect() AttributeError: 'WorkspaceClient' object has no attribute 'connect' ... ``` I am executing the ingestion via the UI (not an external run). The ingestion configuration is very simple and can be found in the attachments. Please note that Metadata Ingestion, Data Lineage, and Data Profiler are all working correctly with the same connection. **To Reproduce** Create the Databricks Unity service as described in [Unity Catalog](https://docs.open-metadata.org/latest/connectors/database/unity-catalog) then set up and run Auto Classification Ingestion on it as outlined in [Adding Auto Classification Ingestion through the UI](https://docs.open-metadata.org/latest/how-to-guides/data-governance/classification/auto/workflow). **Expected behavior** I expect the ingestion to complete successfully, providing classification tags and fetching sample data for Databricks Unity assets. **Version:** - OS: We are running on an AKS cluster; however, I was able to reproduce the issue in a Docker Compose environment as well. - Python version: 3.10 - OpenMetadata version: 1.6.3 - OpenMetadata Ingestion package version: 1.6.3 **Additional context**

title: Speed up display of glossary wit many terms
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When a glossary is displayed, all the terms in the glossary are displayed on a single page. So the more terms there are in the glossary, the longer it takes to display that page. In my case, it takes between 15 and 20 seconds for a glossary of about 800 terms. I understand that glossaries with a flat structure and many terms on the first level are not common, so this is more of a feature request than a bug report. 


**Describe the solution you'd like**

What matters most to me is that the page is displayed faster, independent of the number of terms in the glossary. I suspect that this can best be achieved by pagination or an initial filter.

title: Setting forceEntityOverwriting always leads to MetadataWorkflow failure
body:
**Affected module**
Ingestion Framework

**Describe the bug**
I have a very simple Snowflake ingestion workflow that targets a set of tables. When I set `forceEntityOverwriting` to true in the workflow configuration, it will fail to create with a NoneType error.

**To Reproduce**
This is my workflow
```python
from metadata.workflow.metadata import MetadataWorkflow

workflow_config = {
    "source": {
        "type": "snowflake",
        "serviceName": "abc",
        "sourceConfig": {
            "config": {
                "type": "DatabaseMetadata",
                "markDeletedTables": False,
                "includeTables": True,
                "includeViews": True,
                "includeTags": False,
                "schemaFilterPattern": None,
                "tableFilterPattern": {"includes": ["test*"]},
            }
        },
    },
    "sink": {
        "type": "metadata-rest",
        "config": {},
    },
    "workflowConfig": {
        "openMetadataServerConfig": {
            "hostPort": "yourhosthere",
            "authProvider": "openmetadata",
            "securityConfig": {
                "jwtToken": "yourjwthere",
            },
            "forceEntityOverwriting": True,
        },
        "loggerLevel": "DEBUG",
    },
}
MetadataWorkflow.create(workflow_config)
```

**Expected behavior**
If I set forceEntityOverwriting to true, the code will error with the following call stack.
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "work/test/openmetadata-workflow-test/run.py", line 35, in <module>
    MetadataWorkflow.create(workflow_config)
  File "work/test/openmetadata-workflow-test/.venv/lib64/python3.12/site-packages/metadata/workflow/ingestion.py", line 111, in create
    return cls(config)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "work/test/openmetadata-workflow-test/.venv/lib64/python3.12/site-packages/metadata/workflow/ingestion.py", line 86, in __init__
    super().__init__(
  File "work/test/openmetadata-workflow-test/.venv/lib64/python3.12/site-packages/metadata/workflow/base.py", line 110, in __init__
    self.post_init()
  File "work/test/openmetadata-workflow-test/.venv/lib64/python3.12/site-packages/metadata/workflow/ingestion.py", line 105, in post_init
    self.set_steps()
  File "work/test/openmetadata-workflow-test/.venv/lib64/python3.12/site-packages/metadata/workflow/metadata.py", line 31, in set_steps
    self.source = self._get_source()
                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "work/test/openmetadata-workflow-test/.venv/lib64/python3.12/site-packages/metadata/workflow/metadata.py", line 56, in _get_source
    source: Source = source_class.create(
                     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "work/test/openmetadata-workflow-test/.venv/lib64/python3.12/site-packages/metadata/ingestion/source/database/snowflake/metadata.py", line 195, in create
    connection: SnowflakeConnection = config.serviceConnection.root.config
                                      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

I suspect that it is related to https://github.com/open-metadata/OpenMetadata/blob/main/ingestion/src/metadata/workflow/ingestion.py#L150. If `forceEntityOverwriting` is set to true, the `serviceConnection` object is never initialized. The intent of this is unclear, however.

**Version:**
 - OS: Linux
 - Python version: 3.12
 - OpenMetadata version: 1.5.x, 1.6.x
 - OpenMetadata Ingestion package version: [e.g. `openmetadata-ingestion[docker]==1.5.x/1.6.x`]

title: MSSQL Stored Procedure Metadata Ingestion causes Arithmetic Overflow
body:
**Affected module**
ingestion/src/metadata/ingestion/source/database/mssql/queries.py

**Describe the bug**

The MSSQL_GET_STORED_PROCEDURE_QUERIES  sql code is using the wrong system table to compute stored procedure duration and the wrong unit conversion to seconds (millisec s/b microsec).

The query is using sys.dm_exec_procedure_stats "total_elapsed_time" column to reflect stored proc duration and using it in a DATEADD function to compute end-time.
In addition, it is dividing by 1000 to convert to seconds, but should divide by 1000000.

This column ("total_elapsed_time") is the cumulative time the stored procedure has a accrued over ALL of it's executions, not just the last one.  For a MSSQL server with a long running and frequently executed Stored Procedure, the "total_elapsed_time" value is large enough to cause an Arithmetic Overflow error in the DATEADD function.

Suggest the column that should be used for this is the "last_worker_time" column.

**To Reproduce**

Using an extracted subset of the MSSQL_GET_STORED_PROCEDURE_QUERIES sql:

            select
              s.last_execution_time  start_time,
              s.total_elapsed_time  elapsed_time,
              DATEADD(s, s.total_elapsed_time/1000, s.last_execution_time) end_time,
              OBJECT_NAME(s.object_id, s.database_id) as procedure_name
              from 
                sys.dm_exec_procedure_stats s
              where OBJECT_NAME(s.object_id, s.database_id) IS NOT NULL
              and s.database_id = db_id()
              order by elapsed_time desc
            ;

            -- RESULT
            -- SQL Error [8115] [S0002]: An error occurred during the current command (Done status 0). 
            -- Arithmetic overflow error converting expression to data type int.

Finding the offending Stored Procedure:

            select
              s.last_execution_time  start_time,
              s.total_elapsed_time  elapsed_time,
              -- DATEADD(s, s.total_elapsed_time/1000, s.last_execution_time) end_time,
              OBJECT_NAME(s.object_id, s.database_id) as procedure_name
              from 
                sys.dm_exec_procedure_stats s
              where OBJECT_NAME(s.object_id, s.database_id) not like 'sp_%'
              order by elapsed_time desc
            ;

            2024-12-08 20:00:01.047	**_3431915680349_**	replication_cis
            2024-12-08 20:30:00.497	1063036715221	CIS_TASKS_LOAD
            2024-12-09 02:43:41.597	230498365752	replication_abs
            2024-12-08 21:59:01.030	186063585227	CIS_TASKS_PreProcesses
            2024-12-07 06:02:20.223	149528623548	DatabaseMaintenancePlan
            2024-12-07 05:05:01.013	59591778456	GetSnrStatsForSPU


**Expected behavior**
MSSQL Stored Procedure Metadata would be ingested into OpenMetadata instead of failing on an Arithmetic Overflow error.

**Version:**

 - OS: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS (GNU/Linux 5.4.0-198-generic x86_64)
 - Python version: 3.10.14
 - OpenMetadata version: 1.5.12
 - OpenMetadata Ingestion package version: docker.getcollate.io/openmetadata/ingestion:1.5.12


select @@servername, @@version;
-- SQLSERVER
-- Microsoft SQL Server 2008 R2 (SP3-GDR) (KB4057113) - 10.50.6560.0 (X64) 
--	Dec 28 2017 15:03:48 
--	Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation
--	Standard Edition (64-bit) on Windows NT 6.1 <X64> (Build 7601: Service Pack 1) (Hypervisor)



**Additional context**

Suggested SQL correction:

MSSQL_GET_STORED_PROCEDURE_QUERIES = textwrap.dedent(
    """
WITH SP_HISTORY (start_time, end_time, procedure_name, query_text) AS (
  select 
    s.last_execution_time start_time,
    -- DATEADD(s, s.total_elapsed_time/1000, s.last_execution_time) end_time,
    DATEADD(s, s.last_worker_time/1000000, s.last_execution_time) end_time,
    OBJECT_NAME(object_id, database_id) as procedure_name,
    text as query_text
  from sys.dm_exec_procedure_stats s
  CROSS APPLY sys.dm_exec_sql_text(s.plan_handle)
  WHERE OBJECT_NAME(object_id, database_id) IS NOT NULL
    AND s.last_execution_time > '{start_date}'
),
Q_HISTORY (database_name, query_text, start_time, end_time, duration,query_type, schema_name, user_name) AS (
  select    
    db.NAME database_name,
    t.text query_text,
    s.last_execution_time start_time,
    -- DATEADD(s, s.total_elapsed_time/1000, s.last_execution_time) end_time,
    -- s.total_elapsed_time/1000 duration,
    DATEADD(s, s.last_worker_time/1000000, s.last_execution_time) end_time,
    s.last_worker_time/1000000 duration,
    case
        when t.text LIKE '%%MERGE%%' then 'MERGE'
        when t.text LIKE '%%UPDATE%%' then 'UPDATE'
        when t.text LIKE '%%SELECT%%INTO%%' then 'CREATE_TABLE_AS_SELECT'
        when t.text LIKE '%%INSERT%%' then 'INSERT'
    else 'UNKNOWN' end query_type,
    NULL schema_name,
    NULL user_name
  FROM sys.dm_exec_cached_plans AS p
  INNER JOIN sys.dm_exec_query_stats AS s
    ON p.plan_handle = s.plan_handle
  CROSS APPLY sys.dm_exec_sql_text(p.plan_handle) AS t
  INNER JOIN sys.databases db
    ON db.database_id = t.dbid
  WHERE t.text NOT LIKE '/* {{"app": "OpenMetadata", %%}} */%%'
    AND t.text NOT LIKE '/* {{"app": "dbt", %%}} */%%'
    AND p.objtype NOT IN ('Prepared', 'Proc')
    AND s.last_execution_time > '{start_date}'
)
select 
  Q.query_type AS QUERY_TYPE,
  Q.database_name  AS QUERY_DATABASE_NAME,
  Q.schema_name AS QUERY_SCHEMA_NAME,
  Q.query_text AS QUERY_TEXT,
  Q.user_name AS QUERY_USER_NAME,
  Q.start_time AS QUERY_START_TIME,
  Q.duration AS QUERY_DURATION,
  SP.procedure_name AS PROCEDURE_NAME,
  SP.query_text AS PROCEDURE_TEXT,
  SP.start_time AS PROCEDURE_START_TIME,
  SP.end_time AS PROCEDURE_END_TIME
from SP_HISTORY SP
JOIN Q_HISTORY Q
  ON (
    Q.start_time BETWEEN SP.start_time and SP.end_time
    OR Q.end_time BETWEEN SP.start_time and SP.end_time
    )
order by PROCEDURE_START_TIME desc
;
    """
)
